### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Allow having the global keybind to open directly to a specific extension (including custom installed extensions) instead of the main page

### Scenario when this would be used?

For me personally, I usually just use CmdPal for a few functions like searching my files or most commonly PowerQalc. It's quite annoying that when I start up CmdPal it won't default to PowerQalc, and this is very apparent when I press Enter to copy a result and when I open up CmdPal again it's back on the default page.

I'm sure many members of the community may feel similarly about this

body_text:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

There are 3 ways this could be implemented:

1. **Press the Deactivation Key AFTER down-pressing the letter key.** 
When the Quick Accent popup is activated, pressing a modifier key (like <kbd>Enter</kbd> <kbd>Space</kbd>, or <kbd>Esc</kbd>) should _deactivate_ it, to allow Windows' default Character Repeat behavior to occur. (Note: The modifier key should be intercepted, so e.g. pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd> would NOT send the Enter keyevent to any other window.)
2. **Press the Deactivation Key BEFORE down-pressing the letter key.**
To suppress the Quick Accent popup from activating in the first place, press down a modifier key _before_ the letter key, thereby allowing Character Repeat to occur. (The main challenge I see with this option is to find a key that doesn't already send an (important) keyevent when pressed. Perhaps <kbd>CapsLock</kbd>? It would require intercepting the default <kbd>CapsLock</kbd> keyevent so that system's CapsLock state is changed on key*up*, instead of the default key*down*. That way, to perform a normal CapsLock keypress, the user would press and release <kbd>CapsLock</kbd>, like normal; to use it as the QA Deactivation Key, the user would press down <kbd>CapsLock</kbd>, press and hold down a letter key, then release both. When used as the Deactivation Key, the system CapsLock state should not change.)
3. **Triple-press-then-hold a letter key to suppress QA and trigger "character repeat."**
To suppress Quick Accent from activating, the letter key is quickly pressed 3 times and held down on the 3rd press. Unlike options #[]()1 and #[]()2, No separate modifier key is required. Since the point of Character Repeat is to write the same letter many times, this method basically "gets it started" by making the user type the first 2 manually; when the 3rd one is held down, Character Repeat takes over. (I suggested a *triple*-press-and-hold instead of *double-* in order to reduce the likelihood of accidental triggers. For example, typing the word "continuüm" requires the user `press + press-and-hold` the <kbd>U</kbd> key. However, I think it's very unlikely that a user would need to type the same letter 3 times with an accent on only the last one— aka my proposed action, `press + press + press-and-hold`).

### Scenario when this would be used?

Now that there's an option to activate Quick Accent by simply holding down the key without pressing any second key, it totally disables "character repeat," aka the default Windows behavior when holding down a key.

### Supporting information

This could be integrated with #23496, or it could be a separate key.

That way, to perform a normal CapsLock keypress, the user would press and release <kbd>CapsLock</kbd>, like normal; to use it as the QA Deactivation Key, the user would press down <kbd>CapsLock</kbd>, press and hold down a letter key, then release both. When used as the Deactivation Key, the system CapsLock state should not change.)
3. **Triple-press-then-hold a letter key to suppress QA and trigger "character repeat."**
To suppress Quick Accent from activating, the letter key is quickly pressed 3 times and held down on the 3rd press. Unlike options #[]()1 and #[]()2, No separate modifier key is required. Since the point of Character Repeat is to write the same letter many times, this method basically "gets it started" by making the user type the first 2 manually; when the 3rd one is held down, Character Repeat takes over. (I suggested a *triple*-press-and-hold instead of *double-* in order to reduce the likelihood of accidental triggers. For example, typing the word "continuüm" requires the user `press + press-and-hold` the <kbd>U</kbd> key. However, I think it's very unlikely that a user would need to type the same letter 3 times with an accent on only the last one— aka my proposed action, `press + press + press-and-hold`).

### Scenario when this would be used?

Now that there's an option to activate Quick Accent by simply holding down the key without pressing any second key, it totally disables "character repeat," aka the default Windows behavior when holding down a key.

﻿Right now FancyZones only places a window automatically if it has been snapped before. With "Move newly created windows to their last known zone" on, an app that was previously zoned goes back to its last zone. But the first time you ever open an app, or any app you have never manually snapped, FancyZones does nothing: the window just opens wherever Windows decides to put it, and you drag it into a zone yourself. There is currently no setting anywhere that changes this. For anyone who reinstalls an app, resets their zone history, or just runs a lot of one-off tools and dialogs, this means FancyZones effectively guides only the windows you have already trained it on, and leaves everything else on its own.

I looked through the existing backlog for anything that already covers this and found two issues that are close but not quite the same thing:

- #9527 is about which *layout* gets applied to a monitor or virtual desktop that FancyZones has never seen before. It solves "what grid of zones shows up here" for an unrecognized screen. It says nothing about where an individual window, snapped or not, lands inside whatever layout is already active. A monitor could have a perfectly good layout applied and this proposal would still do nothing, because the gap is per-window, not per-monitor.
- #16964 is about pinning a specific application's remembered zone so it stops drifting between its last few positions. That is a fix for existing history, for apps that already have some. It does not help the very common case of a window with no history at all, which is what this issue is about, and it does not extend to windows generally, only to whichever apps you have explicitly locked.

Both are useful and neither one gives a new window, or one from an app you have never zoned, a default place to go. I think this is worth handling on its own rather than folded into either.

What I would propose, roughly: a per-layout setting, off by default and out of the way (collapsed) so it does not clutter the FancyZones settings page for people who do not want it, that lets you pick either a single zone or a contiguous range of zones as the fallback for that layout. When a window has no last-known-zone to go back to (either because the toggle for that is off, or because this is genuinely the first time), and this fallback is configured and still makes sense for the zone count on that monitor, the window goes there instead of nowhere. If last-known-zone history exists and that toggle is on, history would still win, this is only for the gap that's left over once history has nothing to offer.

I'm not attached to the details here and would rather get the direction right before writing any of it. Two things I'd actually like your input on: does this fit where you want FancyZones settings to go, or do you see this differently? And would you rather this live per layout as I described, or as a single global fallback that applies everywhere regardless of which layout is active? I can see arguments either way and would rather build the one you'd actually want to maintain.

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.99.1

### Installation method

GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

General

### Steps to reproduce

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fae164aa-a8e6-4fbf-a190-e02f0afba023

1. Open PowerToys Settings.
2. Navigate to any module page that has checkboxes inside an expandable group
3. Make sure at least one checkbox in the group is unchecked.
4. Toggle the main Enable switch at the top of the page Off.
5. Toggle it back On.

Every previously unchecked checkbox now displays a dark checkmark artifact inside its box. The box visually looks checked even though it isn't.
Workaround: Navigating away to another module page and back clears the artifact.

This is reproducible on any settings page with checkboxes inside a SettingsGroup (FancyZones, AlwaysOnTop, ColorPicker, etc.).

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Unchecked checkboxes should remain visually empty after the feature is toggled off and back on.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Unchecked checkboxes show a ghost checkmark until the page is refreshed by navigating away and back.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

OS: Windows 11
The artifact only appears after a Disabled to Enabled transition on the parent SettingsGroup.

### Other Software

_No response_

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Currently, it is not possible to remap a single key or special function key to launch an app directly.
Suggestion: Allow certain keys to be remapped to launch an app directly. This could be limited to special function keys.

### Scenario when this would be used?

My keyboard have some special function keys not available on normal keyboards, like favorite, startpage, email, messenger, and other. This special keys have partly not even a function bounded in windows without use of external programs.
For this buttons would be nice if they can directly start an app or shortcut.
If there are any concerns, the feature could possibly be limited to keys that aren't found on a standard keyboard.

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.98.1

### Installation method

WinGet

### Area(s) with issue?

FancyZones

### Steps to reproduce

I really love the feature that snaps new windows in their last known zone. With some applications however, this doesn't always work well:

- Enable the setting to move new windows to their last known zone
- Snap a window into a zone
- Open a new window (while the first one is still open, after it has been closed or after a reboot, it doesn't matter)



### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The new window should snap in the same zone as the manually snapped one

### ❌ Actual Behavior

- Visual Studio 2022/2026 is always offset a few pixels to the right
- Windows Explorer and Windows Terminal moves only to the zone if it is the first window, further concurrent windows just end up somewhere in that region

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

Power Toys is run as normal user.

OS: Windows 11 Enterprise 24H2
OS Language: German (de-DE)
Monitor resolution: 3440x1440 (scaled 100%), landscape
2 more monitors are there with different resolutions, but I use them with fullscreen windows and at least with those (Edge, Outlook, Teams, Chrome) it works

With other applications (e.g. Windows settings, VS Code, Excel, Rider) it works fine :-D

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

- Design a layout by using the Grid layout and then add a free moving "Canvas" zone on top
- Make it possible to convert a Grid layout into a Mixed layout

Optional
- Make it possible to convert a Mixed layout into a Canvas layout
- Make it possible to convert a Canvas layout into a Mixed layout
- Make it possible to convert a Grid layout into a Canvas layout
- Make it possible to convert a Mixed layout into a Grid layout (this would discard the canvas portions)

### Scenario when this would be used?

All of my layouts cover the whole monitor area with no overlap. Some of them though have 2 extra floating slots that overlap with the rest. I can't have these floating slots on the layouts I built using the Grid method.

So... I'd like to have the option to design most of the layout in a grid layout and then just add these extra two areas on all of my layouts

### Supporting information

My personal context: one of the slots is for a Spotify always on top floating player and one 720p area for putting windows on when I'm sharing the screen with people at meetings (because some have 14'' laptops and can't see the stuff I can on my monitor if I share the whole ultra-wide monitor I use)

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

An easy way to define a complex regular expression by giving the desired outcome in natural language. Such as:
Rename all files that look like "Marvels.The.Punisher.S01E01.1080p.NF.Atmos.DDP5.1.HDR.H.265.subrip.eng.ita.esp.mkv"
To "The Punisher S01E01.mkv"

### Scenario when this would be used?

A scenario where you have a lot of files with complex filenames and you want to make the names short and understandable. Generally, whenever you need regex. Mind you, regex isn't something a lot of people are fluent with.

This would actually be one of the rare use cases where LLM integration actually helps the user. Because they haven't got high level understanding of regex syntax. Not only because they are lazy.

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

`main` @ cb25632f (built from source)

### Installation method

Built from source (GitHub)

### Running as admin

No

### Area(s) with issue?

Hosts File Editor

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Hosts File Editor with a large hosts file (e.g. a few thousand entries — blocklist-style hosts files are commonly this size).
2. Note the time spent parsing/loading.
3. Open the add/edit entry dialog and type into the **Address** field.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Address validation is cheap — it's a regex match against a short string.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Validation is far more expensive than the match itself, because a brand new `Regex` is built for every single call.

### Additional Information

`src/modules/Hosts/HostsUILib/Helpers/ValidationHelper.cs`:

```csharp
public static bool ValidIPv6(string address)
{
    if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(address))
    {
        return false;
    }

    var regex = new Regex("^(([0-9a-fA-F]{1,4}:){7,7}[0-9a-fA-F]{1,4}|...");
    return regex.IsMatch(address);
}
```

`ValidIPv4` has the same shape. Neither instance is cached, so on every call the pattern is re-parsed and a fresh matcher is constructed. The IPv6 pattern is **665 characters**, and that construction dominates — the actual `IsMatch` against a short address is trivial by comparison.

Measuring the two patterns against the same .NET regex engine, constructing per call was about **13× slower** than reusing a single instance. (Absolute numbers include the measurement harness's own overhead, so treat the ratio as the meaningful figure.)

This is a hot path:

- `Entry.OnAddressChanged` calls straight into `ValidIPv4`/`ValidIPv6`, so both run **once per entry** while the hosts file is parsed.
- The same property setter fires on **every keystroke** in the address box of the add/edit dialog.

### Proposed fix

Replace both with `[GeneratedRegex]` partial methods. The source generator emits a cached, specialised matcher at compile time — no per-call construction, no runtime pattern parsing — and avoids the reflection-based construction path, which suits the repo's AOT goals. `[GeneratedRegex]` is already used in `OcrTextFormatter`, `ClipboardItemHelper`, `PowerToysShortcutsPopulator` and `DevRibbonViewModel`.

The patterns themselves would carry over byte for byte, so matching behaviour is unchanged and the existing `ValidationHelperTest` suite still applies.

I have this ready and am happy to open a PR if the approach looks right.

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

12.22

### Installation method

Microsoft Store

### Area(s) with issue?

Keyboard Manager

### Steps to reproduce

### 🔴 [FIX] ZoomIt hijacking Ctrl+Z (global Undo) even when inactive

If ZoomIt is stealing your global **Ctrl+Z** shortcut (forcing Draw mode or breaking the Undo command in your IDEs, text editors, or graphic software) even when you are not actively using the app, the issue is caused by a low-level keyboard hook regression triggered by empty (0) hotkey values in the registry. 

### 🔍 The Hidden Behavior (Why it breaks after clicking OK):

Comparing the Windows Registry before and after shows that **the registry values remain 100% identical**. The bug does not corrupt the saved data. Instead, it's a runtime memory issue: when you open ZoomIt's Options dialog and click **OK**, ZoomIt destroys and re-registers its low-level keyboard hooks on the fly. 

If the **DrawToggleKey** is unmapped or left at default fallback values, the hot-reload process gets confused and registers a broad listener that intercepts the un-modified, system-wide Ctrl+Z across the entire OS. Furthermore, upon a normal exit, ZoomIt dumps its current memory state, overwriting any external registry modifications you made while it was open. 

### 🛠️ The Definitive Workaround:

To fix this permanently, you must assign a valid, non-zero shortcut to the standalone drawing tool to satisfy ZoomIt's validation engine, and perform a clean cold launch of the process. 

### Option 1: Manual Registry Fix

1. **Close ZoomIt** completely (Right-click its icon in the system tray and select **Exit**).
2. Press Win + R, type regedit, and hit **Enter**.
3. Navigate to: HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Sysinternals\ZoomIt
4. Modify the DWORD value **DrawToggleKey** and set it to **34b** (Hexadecimal), which maps it to an innocent shortcut (Ctrl+Shift+L).
5. Relaunch **ZoomIt**. *Note: If you ever open the Options dialog and click OK again, the bug will return until the next clean restart.*

### Option 2: Automated Restart Batch Script

Since ZoomIt overwrites the registry on standard exit and breaks when hitting "OK" in the GUI, you can use this quick automation script. It forcefully terminates the process (preventing the registry overwrite dump), restores the safety key, and performs a clean cold launch. 

Create a Restart_ZoomIt.bat file and paste the following code (adjust the path to your executable if necessary): 

cmd

@echo off
title Restart ZoomIt Fix

echo Force closing ZoomIt...
taskkill /f /im ZoomIt64.exe >nul 2>&1
taskkill /f /im ZoomIt.exe >nul 2>&1
timeout /t 1 /nobreak >nul

echo Restoring DrawToggleKey to prevent Ctrl+Z hijacking...
REG ADD "HKCU\Software\Sysinternals\ZoomIt" /v "DrawToggleKey" /t REG_DWORD /d 843 /f >nul

echo Cold launching ZoomIt cleanly...
start "" "C:\Tools\ZoomIt\ZoomIt64.exe"
exit

Use code with caution.

*(Note: 843 is the decimal equivalent of 34b, which maps to Ctrl+Shift+L and keeps your system's global Ctrl+Z perfectly safe).*

FancyZones

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel 0.101.2362 ### Installation method GitHub ### Area(s) with issue? Crop and Lock ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open a browser (Edge/Chrome) and maximize it.
2. Start Crop And Lock and use the Reparent mode (not Thumbnail).
3. Crop a region of the page (e.g. the video player) and confirm.
4. Compare what the Crop And Lock window shows with the region you cropped. ### ✔️ Expected Behavior The Crop And Lock window shows exactly the region that was cropped. ### ❌ Actual Behavior It shows a completely different region (the view is offset by a large amount). Note the key asymmetry: mouse hit-testing is still correct — clicking inside the window lands where the content would be in the original window. Also: Thumbnail mode has no such problem (it does not touch the source window), and File Explorer almost never shows it. ### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file _No response_ ### Additional Information OS version: Windows 11 Pro, 10.0.26200 (Build 26200) .NET version: .NET 10.0.12 (Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App 10.0.12) System Language: Chinese (Simplified) / zh-CN User or System Installation: User Installation (%LOCALAPPDATA%\PowerToys) Running as admin: Yes ### Other Software Microsoft Edge 153.0.4234.32 (Chromium) — reproduced Expected to reproduce in any Chromium-based browser (Chrome/Electron apps), because the issue is about client-area driven layout. Thumbnail mode is unaffected.

body_text:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

In the PowerToys Command Palette settings, the section "Extensions" contains an entry called "Manage fallback order". From a user perspective, this suggests that the fallback order controls the priority or ordering of all extensions, including third-party plugins.

However, the fallback order only applies to command providers (ShellExecute, PATH, app protocols, Windows apps, PowerToys commands). Plugins such as PaletteShell do not appear in this list because they are not command providers and therefore cannot be prioritized.

This UI structure is confusing. Users expect installed extensions to appear in the fallback list. When they do not appear, it looks like a bug or installation issue. The fact that this is "works as designed" is not obvious. The UI creates an incorrect expectation about what can be configured.

Suggested improvements:

- Split the Extensions section into "Plugins" (non-prioritizable) and "Command providers" (prioritizable).

- Rename "Manage fallback order" to something more precise, such as "Command provider priority" or "Fallback order of command sources".

- Add an explanatory note: "Plugins are functional extensions and do not participate in the fallback order."

- Display plugins separately or in a disabled/greyed-out list to indicate that they cannot be reordered.

Why this matters:
The current UI leads users to believe they are doing something wrong or that the software is malfunctioning. A clearer separation between plugins and command providers would improve usability and prevent misunderstandings.

### Scenario when this would be used?

When users install additional Command Palette extensions (e.g., third‑party plugins like PaletteShell), they expect these extensions to appear in the fallback order list and to be reorderable. The current UI suggests that all extensions are covered by the fallback order, which leads users to believe something is wrong when their plugin does not appear. A clearer UI would help users understand when and why fallback ordering applies.

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362 - Stable

### Installation method

Microsoft Store

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

1. Two PCs are connected to the same LAN.

MAIN PC:
- Windows 10
- Hostname: HeadOffice-I7
- Physical keyboard and mouse are connected to this PC.

REMOTE PC:
- Windows 11
- Hostname: DESKTOP-BBPG03H
- PowerToys Mouse Without Borders has "Use Service" enabled.
- PowerToys was run as Administrator when enabling the service.

2. Reboot the Windows 11 remote PC.

3. Wait at the Windows login/password screen without logging in.

4. The Windows 11 PC is already connected to the network and responds normally to ping, but Mouse Without Borders cannot control it.

5. At this stage TCP ports 15100 and 15101 on the Windows 11 PC are not listening/reachable.

6. Log into the Windows 11 PC using its local physical mouse/keyboard.

7. Immediately after login, Mouse Without Borders starts automatically, ports 15100 and 15101 become available, and the Windows 10 PC can control it normally.

Important: After Windows has logged in once, pressing Win+L works correctly and Mouse Without Borders CAN control the Windows lock screen.

Already verified:
- Use Service is enabled.
- PowerToys was genuinely running elevated when Use Service was enabled.
- PowerToys.MWB.Service exists and runs as LocalSystem.
- Service startup type is the default DEMAND_START.
- Service binary path is correct.
- The service was deleted and recreated through PowerToys.
- Firewall and network connectivity are working.
- Both PCs communicate normally after login.
- Security key and machine configuration are correct.
- No machine-level PowerToys policy exists under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\PowerToys disabling the feature.
- The Windows 10 PC is already running Mouse Without Borders before login and repeatedly attempts to connect to the Windows 11 PC.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

With "Use Service" enabled, Mouse Without Borders should allow the Windows 10 PC to control the Windows 11 PC at the Windows login/password screen immediately after a fresh boot, before the first user login.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

After a fresh boot, Mouse Without Borders does not work at the Windows 11 login/password screen.

It only becomes available after I log into the Windows 11 PC locally for the first time.

After that first login, Mouse Without Borders works normally, including on the lock screen after pressing Win+L.

This appears very similar to PowerToys issue #29060.

Could you please confirm whether controlling the Windows login screen immediately after a fresh boot is currently supported by Mouse Without Borders Service?

If yes, what should start or trigger PowerToys.MWB.Service before the first user login?

If this is a known bug, is there currently a fix or supported workaround?

I can provide PowerToys diagnostic logs if required.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[PowerToysReport_2026-09-22-11-13-07.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32505174/PowerToysReport_2026-09-22-11-13-07.zip)

### Additional Information

Remote PC (affected machine):
Windows 11
Hostname: DESKTOP-BBPG03H
PowerToys version: 0.101.2362 Stable
Installation: Microsoft Store
Mouse Without Borders "Use Service": ON
PowerToys.MWB.Service account: LocalSystem
Service startup type: DEMAND_START

Main PC:
Windows 10
Hostname: HeadOffice-I7
Physical keyboard and mouse are connected to this PC.

The attached PowerToysReport ZIP was generated on the affected Windows 11 remote PC.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Currently, the Keyboard Manager "Open URL" action type supports only a single URL per shortcut mapping. Users who want to open multiple URLs simultaneously (e.g., a set of work-related tabs) must create separate mappings with different shortcut keys for each URL.

Proposed behavior: Allow the "Open URL" action to accept multiple URLs (one per line). When the shortcut is triggered, all listed URLs open at once in the default browser.

The URL input TextBox in the remapping dialog would become multi-line (similar to the existing "Text" action type), and each line would be treated as a separate URL to open. The engine would iterate through each URL and call ShellExecute for each one.

Example:

Shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + W
URLs:

https://mail.google.com
https://calendar.google.com
https://github.com/notifications
Result: All three URLs open in the default browser when the shortcut is pressed.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Scenario when this would be used?
Morning workflow launch: Many power users start their day by opening the same set of websites — email, calendar, project boards, dashboards. Currently this requires either:

Multiple separate KBM shortcut mappings (wastes shortcut combinations)
A browser extension or bookmark folder (not keyboard-driven)
A batch script mapped to a shortcut (extra complexity)
With multi-URL support, a single shortcut like Ctrl+Alt+W could open an entire "workspace" of URLs instantly. This is especially valuable for:

Context switching — Switch between "work" and "personal" tab sets with different shortcuts
Project-specific setups — Open all relevant dashboards/docs for a specific project
Presentation prep — Open demo URLs before a meeting
Development workflows — Open local dev server, API docs, and CI dashboard together

### Supporting information

Technical feasibility
The change is backward-compatible and minimally invasive. The existing uriToOpen string field can store newline-delimited URLs without requiring changes to:

The P/Invoke interop boundary
The C++/CLI wrapper layer
The JSON settings schema (the "openUri" key already stores a string)


Affected module
Keyboard Manager — New Editor UI (KeyboardManagerEditorUI)
Specifically the "Open URL" action type in shortcut remapping

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

An enhanced Auto-hide feature for the Command Palette Dock with the ability to change the size of the edge sensitive to mouse hover that shows the dock. 
It should be like the Samsung side-bar feature in which the user can change the size and position of the bar.

### Scenario when this would be used?

When using apps that have back arrows of close boxes in areas the dock edge is makes it hard to click the button. If the edge size were smaller, the user could adjust where they want the edge to be so that when they hover their mouse pointer over buttons they need to use, the dock won't show when they don't want it to.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

A system can have multiple GPUs, Networks, and disks.  The current widgets for the Dock only allow the user to pin the whole "Perfromance Monitor" widget or the individual ones.  This feature would allow multipleof the same type of widget to be pinned, so that they can each be set to track different objects.

### Scenario when this would be used?

On a devices that have
- Multiple networks (Ethernet, WiFi, and Virtual Ethernets for VMs)
- Multiple disks (https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/releases/tag/v0.101.2362.0 added my feature for showing disk stats in the performance monitor
- Multiple GPUs

Where users want to monitor/test thing and not have to constantly cycle though the one widget.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

**Dear Zoom It Team,**
I have installed Zoom It v12.22 and tested the font Khmer Unicode, but it doesn't show correctly. 
When I press T for typing and switch the keyboard to Khmer, then type. I consent to show, but the vowels are not shown correctly.
I hope you can fix it and release a new version very soon.
Thank you in advance.
Best regards,
Kimsorn

### Scenario when this would be used?

Ctrl + 2 > When I press T for typing and switch the keyboard to Khmer, then type. I consent to show, but the vowels are not shown correctly.

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.1012632

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

Power Display

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable and activate Power Display and the `Show rotation control` setting under any monitor.
2. Use the `Rotation control` feature to digitally flip your monitor to either Portrait or Horizontal (flipped).
3. Notice how the mouse cursor's _displayed_ X and Y coordinates are not inverted, even though it mathematically is.
4. (Optional/Results may vary) Use a recording system such as OBS (using Display Capture) to get a better picture on the issue.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The mouse coordinates should properly reflect the screen's rotation.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The mouse's mathematical position updated properly, while the visual position became desynced.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[PowerDisplay.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32547006/PowerDisplay.log)

### Additional Information


| Setting Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| OS | Windows 11 Pro |
| .NET | 4.8.09221 |
| Language | English only |
| Installation Type | System-wide |
| Administrator | No |

body_text: ### Description of the new feature / enhancement Workspaces have a lot of potential, it could improve navegation wise and feature wise: 1- **Minimize or close ALL WINDOWS**: would be huge, is really anoying open 20 windows and if you want to minimize all that you have to go one by one (as well to close them) 2- **Subcategories**: Right now every workspace has its applications and layout and CLI to pass arguments to the apps (to open specific documents etc), if you are working on 3 diferent lets say SONGS and applications and layouts are exaclty the same, right now you have to create N number of workspaces and the only change is the CLI for the apps. I think is better to have a set of apps and layouts and a list (subcategories) with the diferent CLI for every app and of course show them as subcategory on the Workspace editor 3- **Create a hide bar tool bar on top**: Having the " Win + ctr + ` " short cut is great but imagine this: you place your pointer on top or any border the user wants the bar to be, the bar pops up showing you the diferent workspaces as the current task bar. 3.1-**Get advantage of virtual desktops**: Using the idea on point 3 you can set different workspaces to different virtual desktops lets say you have: Personal, Develop, Music, Games Desktops, if you click on a "Music" Workspace those are going to be open on the corresponding desktop, the WORKSPACE BAR would be available in any desktop and it would allow change between workspaces of different desktops through 2 arrows, once you select your workspace it would be open and the virtual desktop would be selected: ### Scenario when this would be used? EVERY DAY USE literally this could arrange and save alot of space fot any user in any moment ### Supporting information _No response_

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Sometimes the minimum brightness of a monitor is still brighter than preferred. And some applications are brighter than others.

A transparent window with variable opacity overlaid on top of the screen/window can reduce the brightness of a screen *beyond* and DDC/DC brightness control support - or on monitors that do not support DDC/CI.

Suggested details about the proposed implementation:
* Add Overlay Profile support defining overlay transparency percentage increments or specific percentage levels (like how custom VCP names can be defined currently). Default setting would be a 5%, 10% or 25% increment.
* Applying predefined overlay transparency profiles to 1 or more monitors. Overlay will only function on monitors where it has been applied.
* Monitor overlay type 1 - Allow overlay transparency dimming to be applied *after* reaching minimum brightness (for "negative" brightness settings) if enabled
* Monitor overlay type 2 - Allow overlay transparency dimming to be managed separately from monitor brightness
* Monitor overlay transparency would probably be either as negative brightness (type 1) or as a separate setting (type 2) - not both.
* Overlay type and overlay profile application would be implemented under the monitor setting. Presumably a checkbox to enable, a combobox to select type 1 vs type 2, and a combo box to apply the defined overlay profiles.
* Full-screen support and region support (e.g. everything except the taskbar, or for zones defined in fancy zones for e.g. ultrawide monitors)
* Possible overlay application to the current foreground window with hotkeys or even a slider for the current application. That would terminate when the window terminates. I think you can, to a degree, make another window be the parent of your window by obtaining the handle through the Win32 API. So you should be able to capture events on that without too much pain.
* Potential setting for overlay color - helpful sometimes for visibility, though it overlaps with color space and blue/yellow light settings

An initial implementation would be a full per-monitor overlay with 5%, 10% or 25% increments with a separate slider bar (not integrated with brightness). Both the overlay profile and the default overlay transparency setting could be saved in the profile.


### Scenario when this would be used?

Monitors that don't support DDC/CI could still have partial brightness support with a transparent overlay
Monitors with DDC/CI support that are still relatively bright when at 0% brightness could be further dimmed
Setups with multiple monitors from multiple vendors will have different physical brightness values when set to 0% brightness. A transparent overlay could bring the brighter monitors in line with the dimmest ones.

### Supporting information

Parts of this could conceivable be implemented externally. For _window_ and region overlays, it would make as much sense to have that implemented externally as internally - except if you want to share overlay increment profiles between them.

For the monitor-specific overlays, I'd argue that placing it within Power Display makes the most sense. It helps compensate for monitors with poor DDC/CI support, could be enabled on any or all monitors, and could be managed within profiles to give the perfect brightness setting

There are multiple tools that do this already - just like there are tools that do what Power Display does. But there aren't good tools that do both DDC/CI brightness control _and_ transparent overlay control. And Power Display's profile support would make it especially useful.

Fullscreen applications, UAC and lock screens may not be affected by transparent overlays.

Transparent overlays can never fully replace brightness settings, as the backlight is unaffected by the overlay and it can never reach true black. But it can have enough of a difference for people with sensitive eyes or dark environments to make consistent use of it. And the ability to normalize monitor brightness with it is also helpful.

Some sample applications that do things like this could be **darkbright-helper** or **MonitorDimmer** (both on Github). **darkbright-helper** uses the "negative brightness" concept, where it changes hardware brightness until you hit 0, and then when you go lower, it dims by applying a transparent overlay.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

The Mouse Highlighter circle should automatically adjust its rendered pixel radius based on the active monitor's display scaling (DPI) factor.

Currently, the highlighter radius appears to use a fixed pixel count. On multi-monitor setups where monitors have different zoom levels (e.g., 100% scale on Display 1 vs. 150% or 200% scale on Display 2), moving the cursor from one screen to another causes the highlight circle to visually shrink or grow significantly relative to the rest of the UI elements on that screen.

Proposed Behavior:
Scale the rendering radius dynamically using the current display's DPI scale factor (Radius * (Current_DPI / Base_DPI)) so the highlight maintains a consistent visual scale relative to on-screen UI across all displays.

### Scenario when this would be used?

This is critical for anyone using multi-monitor setups with mixed display scales (e.g., a high-DPI laptop screen paired with standard 1080p/4K external monitors).

Without DPI normalization, the highlighter is either too small to notice on high-density displays or awkwardly oversized on lower-density displays, creating an inconsistent visual feedback experience when presenting, recording video tutorials, or navigating across screens.

### Supporting information

- Observed: Moving the mouse cursor between a 100% scaled monitor and a 150%/200% scaled monitor results in noticeable size discrepancies in the highlight overlay circle.
- Applies to: PowerToys Mouse Utilities -> Mouse Highlighter.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Currently, PowerToys Keyboard Manager restricts per-app remapping to the "Remap Shortcuts" module, which strictly validates input to require a modifier key (e.g., Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Win). Users cannot directly assign a single physical key (e.g., End) to execute an app-specific action (e.g., Ctrl+W in chrome.exe). While a manual two-step workaround exists (mapping the single key to a complex dummy shortcut globally, then mapping that dummy shortcut to the target action per-app), this creates significant friction.

I am requesting an automated bridge for this workaround, alongside several cohesive UX improvements to modernize the Keyboard Manager module:

Automated Single-Key Per-App Routing: Allow users to select a single key in a per-app context. The UI should silently abstract the manual workaround by automatically generating and assigning an internal dummy shortcut (e.g., an unused Virtual Key sequence) to route the single keypress to the target app.

Interactive Capture UX: Ensure the physical Select keystroke capture button is consistently available across all input fields so users are not forced to scroll through the VK dropdown list when configuring app-specific rules.

Terminology & Disclaimers: Provide inline tooltips explaining technical terms like "Chords" (two-step key sequences) and "VK Codes" (Virtual Key codes). Additionally, include inline warnings clarifying that active-window hooking (GetForegroundWindow checks on WH_KEYBOARD_LL) introduces minor input latency, explicitly advising against using per-app single-key remappings for latency-critical applications like competitive gaming.

Metadata Fields: Introduce Created Date/Timestamp and Notes/Description fields for every active remapping rule to document the business logic or purpose behind specific custom mappings.

Export/Import Support: Enable saving and loading configurations as .json or .md files for deployment across workstations and sharing with colleagues.

Community Presets / Command Palette: Integrate a repository of popular productivity remappings that can be applied via checkboxes or deployed dynamically via PowerToys Run.

### Scenario when this would be used?

This functionality addresses standard productivity workflows where a user wants to repurpose a single, accessible hardware key (like End, Insert, or a dedicated macro key) to perform a specific function (like closing a tab or muting audio) exclusively within a target application (like Chrome or Teams), without breaking the key's native functionality system-wide.

The metadata, export capabilities, and clear terminology allow power users to document complex mapping logic, share standardized workflows across a corporate team or multi-device setup, and prevent configurations from becoming "black boxes" months after creation.

### Supporting information

Note regarding template constraints: While this issue contains multiple feature requests, they collectively address a single overarching objective: eliminating the UX friction of the Keyboard Manager's current input validation rules and bridging the gap between power-user capabilities and non-power-user accessibility.

The underlying system architecture for the single-key per-app mapping already works via the manual chaining method. Automating the dummy shortcut generation within the UI parser requires no changes to the low-level keyboard hook mechanism itself, keeping performance overhead identical to current implementations. Furthermore, allowing physical key capture in the shortcut fields mitigates user confusion when encountering the VK code dropdown list.

### Installation method

WinGet

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

. Open Mouse Without Borders settings
2. Go to the encryption key section
3. Manually type security key + device name
4. Click "Connect"
5. Fields are wiped instantly, no connection happens, no error shown, typed values are lost

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

- Manually entered field values must NEVER be cleared automatically by the app, regardless of connection outcome.
- Connection attempt should proceed (port is confirmed reachable), or show a clear error, and values should stay in the fields so the user can retry or fix them.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

User-entered data is wiped immediately, connection drops silently, feature unusable. No log file found to attach — would be happy to provide one if the app produced it.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

### Version
v0.101.2362 windows 11

### Description
In Mouse Without Borders, in the encryption key section, entering a value in the security key field and device name field and clicking the inline "Connect" button immediately WIPES both fields without connecting and without any way to retry with the same values.

**This is the core problem: fields the user manually typed must never be cleared automatically, especially not on a failed/incomplete action.** Losing manually entered data with no confirmation and no way to recover it is a basic UX violation, not just a connection bug.

### Troubleshooting already done
- Disabled Windows Firewall entirely — same result.
- Test-NetConnection 192.168.1.137 -Port 15101 -> succeeds (TcpTestSucceeded: True), so the target port is reachable and it's not a network/firewall issue.

body_text: ### Description of the new feature / enhancement Add an option in Command Palette Settings to change the layout/view mode for browsing files and folders. The requested view options include: - Extra large icons - Large icons - Medium icons - Small icons - List view This will allow users to customize how items are displayed based on their preference and workflow needs. ### Scenario when this would be used? When searching or browsing media files (like images, designs, or video assets) inside Command Palette, having larger icon views helps to preview the content visually without opening each file. On the other hand, switching to a compact List view allows users to see more file details and search results at once on screen without scrolling too much. ### Supporting information Currently, Command Palette uses a fixed layout format. Adding Explorer-like view options directly in the Command Palette settings would make navigating local files much more efficient.

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2652 (preview)

### Installation method

GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

Keyboard Manager

### Steps to reproduce

Create a shortcut with Alt + J as Trigger, Down key press as Action

Open notepad and add a few lines, then move to the top of the file. Press Alt + J

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The cursor should move down a line as the down key is pressed

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The Alt menu is triggered, displaying the key presses required to open the File, Edit, View menu etc.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

I realize that this may be an accessibility thing, but if I specifically go out of my way to create a shortcut overriding Alt + J then I understand that I lose the ability to hit that combination for Alt menus. As it stands, Alt chords are not really useful.

Ideally if in my example I press Alt + F, it would still open the file menu.

I have gotten this to work in my own keyboard shortcut software by sending the following inputs when I see that a shortcut has been triggered:

1. Dummy key (key code 0xFF) down
2. Dummy key up
3. Trigger key(s) up (in this case J)
4. Modifier key(s) up (in this case Alt)
5. Action key(s) down (Down in this case)
6. Action key(s) up
7. Modifier key(s) down (So that Alt is still being held down after the shortcut fires)
8. Dummy key down
9. Dummy key up

This allowed the Alt menu to work with other keys, while preventing it from appearing for bound Alt key chords. This sequence may or may not cause issues in certain cases in your software, but if it does maybe it could be special cased specifically for Alt key chords bound to key press actions.

body_text: ### Description of the new feature / enhancement In the FancyZones Editor, there is a small part of the UI dedicated to selecting which monitor you want to apply a layout to. The values assigned to the displays appear to be arbitrary. What I propose is to match the display identifiers in the FancyZones Editor to be the same as the display identifiers used in Windows Display settings. For example, I have three monitors. In Windows display settings, it is simple, going left to right my displays are identified as 1 -> 2 -> 3. Those same displays in PowerToys, going left to right, are identified as 3 -> 1 -> 2. ### Scenario when this would be used? Every time you edit or change your layout desired for a display. ### Supporting information

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2632

### Installation method

GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

Command Palette

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable the Command Palette Dock and pin one or more commands/extensions to the Center region.
2. Restart Command Palette (or restart the system / relaunch PowerToys).
3. Observe the Dock.
4. Items pinned to the Center region do not render automatically.
5. Right-click the Dock background and select "Edit Dock" (without making any changes), then exit edit mode.
6. The Center items now appear correctly.

This happens on every fresh launch of Command Palette / the Dock — it is not a one-time occurrence.

Note: Items pinned to the Start and End regions load correctly and consistently. The issue appears to be isolated to the Center region specifically.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb3633d4-c047-44c6-9099-45654342be69

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Command Palette Dock should render all pinned items in all three regions (Start, Center, End) automatically on load, without requiring the user to manually enter and exit Edit Dock mode.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Items pinned to the Center region are missing/not rendered until Edit Dock mode is opened once (with no changes made), after which they display correctly — until the next relaunch, when the issue recurs.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

Dock position: Top
OS version: Windows 11 26H1 / 10.0.28000.3086
This appears to be a loading/initialization issue specific to the Center band of the Dock, separate from the Start and End bands which are unaffected.

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0

### Installation method

WinGet

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Utilities

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install PowerToys **0.101.2362.0**.
2. Enable **Mouse Jump**.
3. Press `Shift + Alt + A`.
4. The Mouse Jump preview window appears normally.
5. Click any location in the Mouse Jump preview window.


### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Clicking a location in the Mouse Jump preview should move the mouse cursor to the corresponding location, as expected from the Mouse Jump functionality.


### ❌ Actual Behavior

The Mouse Jump preview window appears normally, but **mouse clicks have no effect at all**.

Clicking anywhere in the preview does not move the cursor and does not appear to trigger any action.

There is:

* No error message
* No warning
* No crash
* No visible indication of an error

The Mouse Jump preview simply remains unresponsive to mouse clicks.


### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[PowerToysReport_2026-09-26-01-28-01.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32673702/PowerToysReport_2026-09-26-01-28-01.zip)

### Additional Information

## Mouse Jump preview window does not respond to mouse clicks in v0.101.2362.0

### Microsoft PowerToys version

**0.101.2362.0**

### Release channel

Preview

### Installation method

WinGet update

### Area(s) with issue

Mouse Utilities / Mouse Jump

### Windows version

* Windows 11 Pro
* Version 25H2
* OS Build 26200.9457

### Hardware

* CPU: Intel Core i5-12400
* GPU: Intel Arc A380
* RAM: 32 GB
* Displays: 3

### Display configuration

The PC uses three displays.

* Display 1 and Display 3 are duplicated/mirrored.
* Display 2 is positioned to the right of the duplicated displays.

### Mouse Jump configuration

* Mouse Jump: Enabled
* Activation shortcut: `Shift + Alt + A`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install PowerToys **0.101.2362.0**.
2. Enable **Mouse Jump**.
3. Press `Shift + Alt + A`.
4. The Mouse Jump preview window appears normally.
5. Click any location in the Mouse Jump preview window.

### Expected behavior

Clicking a location in the Mouse Jump preview should move the mouse cursor to the corresponding location, as expected from the Mouse Jump functionality.

### Actual behavior

The Mouse Jump preview window appears normally, but **mouse clicks have no effect at all**.

Clicking anywhere in the preview does not move the cursor and does not appear to trigger any action.

There is:

* No error message
* No warning
* No crash
* No visible indication of an error

The Mouse Jump preview simply remains unresponsive to mouse clicks.

### Reproducibility

The problem was **100% reproducible** with PowerToys 0.101.2362.0.

### Regression test

I downgraded PowerToys from **0.101.2362.0** to **0.100.2** using the official PowerToys installer.

With PowerToys **0.100.2**, using the same Mouse Jump configuration and the same hardware/display configuration:

1. Press `Shift + Alt + A`.
2. Mouse Jump opens normally.
3. Click a location in the preview.
4. The mouse cursor moves to the clicked location correctly.

The behavior therefore changes between **0.100.2** and **0.101.2362.0**.

### Important comparison

The only change made between the failing and working tests was:

* Uninstall PowerToys 0.101.2362.0
* Install PowerToys 0.100.2

No Windows settings or other system settings were intentionally changed between the tests.

This makes the version difference particularly useful for reproducing the regression.

### Additional information

PowerToys 0.101.2362.0 was installed/updated through WinGet.

PowerToys 0.100.2 was installed using the official PowerToys installer.

I do not know whether PowerToys 0.101.2362.0 was running with administrator privileges.

No error dialog, warning, or crash occurred when the mouse clicks failed.

### Summary

**0.101.2362.0:**
Mouse Jump opens, but mouse clicks in the preview window do nothing.

**0.100.2:**
Mouse Jump opens and mouse clicks correctly move the cursor to the selected location.

The issue appears to be a regression introduced between these versions.

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2652.0 (updated from 0.100.2)

### Installation method

GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install / update to PowerToys 0.101.2652.0 (per-user, x64) on Windows 11 25H2 (26200.9550; also reproduced on 26200.9445).
2. Open Settings > Mouse Without Borders.
3. Click "New key" to generate a new security key, or try to connect to another machine.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

A new security key is generated and MWB settings sync with the running MWB process.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Nothing happens. The Settings log repeats the following about every 0.5 s (11,240 times in one day), starting from the very first launch after the update:

```
[Error] MouseWithoutBordersViewModel.cs::GetSettingsSyncHelperAsync::368
    Couldn't create SettingsSync: System.UnauthorizedAccessException: Rejected SettingsSync server: untrusted-signature
```

It happens both with "Use Service" on (MWB running as LocalSystem) and off (MWB running as the user).

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

OS version: Windows 11 25H2 26200.9550 (x64)
Running as admin: Yes

### Analysis
The Authenticode signer certificates differ between Settings and the MWB binaries in the same 0.101.2652.0 install:

| File | Signer thumbprint | Serial |
|---|---|---|
| PowerToys.exe | AB172913A2960A224809EE8A0C371CD47A079B72 | 330000021D4D19C84ED70F574800000000021D |
| WinUI3Apps\PowerToys.Settings.exe | AB172913A2960A224809EE8A0C371CD47A079B72 | 330000021D4D19C84ED70F574800000000021D |
| PowerToys.MouseWithoutBorders.exe | 1D77A9B9E8FE2075D9AD15123257FB90DB0DA4A1 | 330000021CFACDC59BE82F7EC400000000021C |
| PowerToys.MouseWithoutBordersHelper.exe | 1D77A9B9E8FE2075D9AD15123257FB90DB0DA4A1 | 330000021CFACDC59BE82F7EC400000000021C |
| PowerToys.MouseWithoutBordersService.exe | 1D77A9B9E8FE2075D9AD15123257FB90DB0DA4A1 | 330000021CFACDC59BE82F7EC400000000021C |

- Both certificates are `CN=Microsoft Corporation`, issued by `Microsoft Code Signing PCA 2024`. `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` reports `Valid`, and the chain builds with `X509RevocationMode.Offline`.
- Across the whole install directory, all files are FileVersion 0.101.2652.0 (built 2026-09-23), but 371 files are signed with `AB1729…` and 196 files with `1D77A9…`.
- The installer I used is the official release asset: `PowerToysUserSetup-0.101.2652.0-x64.exe`, SHA256 `0D2BEF1B473F332477BF58426FE09E81439B240687073CA38FB03BDE447A1666`, which matches both the asset digest and the hash table in the release notes.
- In `NamedPipePeerVerification.cs` at tag v0.101.2652.0 (added in #50480, shipped since v0.101.2572.0), `MeetsSigningPolicy` requires `HaveSameTrustedMicrosoftSigner(ownImagePath, peerImagePath)` when the caller has an embedded signature, and the signers are compared as leaf certificates: `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals(firstSigner.RawData, secondSigner.RawData)`. Settings (`AB1729…`) therefore rejects the MWB process (`1D77A9…`) as `untrusted-signature`.
- In 0.101.2362.0, `PowerToys.exe`, `PowerToys.Settings.exe`, and `PowerToys.MouseWithoutBorders.exe` are all signed with `1D77A9…`, and MWB works.

### Workaround
Downgrade to 0.101.2362.0 (uninstall, remove the leftover `%LOCALAPPDATA%\PowerToys` folder, reinstall 0.101.2362.0).

### Suggestion
Either sign all binaries of a release with the same certificate, or compare the signer by a stable identity (for example, the issuing CA chain plus the subject) instead of the leaf certificate.

### Related
- #50480 (introduced the settings-sync peer verification)
- #49949 (Validate settings sync peers)
- #50615 (Settings rejected as `not-microsoft-signed`; different cause, same area of signature verification)

### Other Software

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

V0.96.1

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

FancyZones

### Steps to reproduce

After enabling the Snap Pages / Layout Design feature in PowerToys, the flash/overlay message that Windows normally shows when switching between virtual desktops with Ctrl+Win+Right/Left Arrow stopped appearing. Before enabling those PowerToys feature, the overlay displayed correctly.

Steps to reproduce:

Enable the Snap Pages / Layout Design feature in PowerToys.
Press Ctrl+Win+Right Arrow (or Left Arrow) to switch virtual desktops.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The native Windows overlay indicating the desktop switch should appear.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The overlay no longer appears.

I disabled the "Override Windows Snap" setting in PowerToys, but the overlay still doesn't appear. I'm confident this is related to PowerToys/Snap in general, but I haven't been able to pinpoint which specific setting is causing it.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

OS Name	Microsoft Windows 11 Pro
Version	10.0.26100 Build 26100

Powertoys V0.96.1

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Hi Guys

Been using Powertoys on my PC for a long time and loved it. I recently bought the XBOX ALLY X and with the XBOX mode also available on desktop PC I think this is a good time to introduce some features to make it work better during XBOX mode.

I have a Flydigi vader 5 Pro which supports **dongle** and **bluetooth** as well. With the dongle mode you can use the Flydigi App to map keyboard keys to the controller. I usually set the Shortcut on PowerToys to a specific key (F3..) then apply that key to the controller with the Flydigi App. Everything works great right?... _Thats only using the dongle_.

IF i setup the controller or any Gamepad through BLUETOOTH, we do not have a way to set the shortcuts on PowerToys to a gamepad button because PowerToys doesn't recognize Gamepads. It would be great if We could set the same Shortcuts that we created in PowerToys and when it prompts us to press the keyboard button to attach it to... we could instead press the Gamepad button.


### Scenario when this would be used?

This would solve major problems in XBOX MODE with Gamepads when we need to set TASK VIEW shortcuts to a specific button or the Xbox Gamebar shortcut to another.

For example, The Flydigi Vader 5 Pro has Gamebar mapped to the Home button, but it doesnt have **_Task View_** pre mapped on the controller so there is no way to switch between apps when using a Gamepad in XBOX MODE. I think this is a major request since future XBOX consoles will be PCs.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

When using a laptop in tablet mode (where the keyboard is physically folded behind the screen, such as on a Lenovo Yoga), you must disable the Keyboard Manager shortcuts intended for external keyboard use.
When the laptop is returned to standard mode, the Keyboard Manager shortcuts will be re-enabled.

### Scenario when this would be used?

A status change that happens automatically, instead of me having to manually turn the Keyboard Manager shortcuts on and off.

### Supporting information

Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\PriorityControl" -Name ConvertibleSlateMode
0 - Tablet / Slate
1 - Laptop / Clamshell

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I am requesting a dedicated standalone screen drawing/annotation feature in PowerToys that functions independently of ZoomIt. 

The proposed feature should:
1. Allow users to enter a free-form "Draw Mode" anywhere on the screen using a clean, customizable shortcut.
2. Provide simple on-screen or quick keyboard controls to change line colors and brush thickness.
3. Automatically clear all annotations and reset the cursor state completely upon pressing the shortcut again or hitting 'Esc'.
4. Include support for drawing perfect straight lines (e.g., by holding Shift) for professional presentation callouts and technical charting.


### Scenario when this would be used?

This feature is highly requested for two major everyday workflows:
1. Live Presentations & Education: Instantly highlighting or pointing out specific elements on the screen to an audience without needing full screen magnification or dealing with ZoomIt's broader presentation configurations.
2. Financial Charting & Trading: Quickly drawing free-hand patterns, support/resistance levels, or trendlines over real-time live trading charts, and instantly resetting the screen once the technical analysis or pattern identification is complete.

Currently, ZoomIt bundles drawing with magnification behaviors which often creates configuration friction or causes compatibility/performance issues on certain laptop displays. A separate, lightweight utility dedicated entirely to screen annotation would be much more reliable and streamlined.


### Supporting information

I attempted to use ZoomIt for this purpose, but it failed to function properly on my laptop hardware. Having a modular, standalone application specifically built for screen drawing would provide a lightweight, modern, and robust solution for power users who don't need or want the full ZoomIt overhead.

body_text:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

An option to make any screen annotations made with ZoomIt Draw and Live Zoom become saved so that the next time activated, one will see their previous annotations.  

### Scenario when this would be used?

All of these are real scenarios I have run into where I have seriously wanted this feature:
1. Using draw to write algebra/equations for a math problem, and then wanting to switch to reading something on the computer like a textbook, but not wanting to lose all progress with the problem at hand
2. If annotations were made to fill in a graph of some sort for an assignment, screenshotting, and then turning draw off to submit the created graph, but then realizing afterward that an important feature of the graph is missing. Draw or Live Zoom would then be turned back on and the previous annotations would be re-displayed.
3. Accidentally closing out of Draw/Live Zoom before screenshotting the desired annotated screen.
4. Accidentally cutting off the screenshot of the annotated region of the screen 

### Supporting information

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0 - Preview

### Installation method

Machine-wide installer

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

1. On machine A, copy a file, or more than 1 MB of text.
2. Within 30 seconds, switch to machine B with its Ctrl+Alt+F1..F4 hotkey.
3. Paste on B.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The content is pasted, as it is when you switch by moving the mouse to B.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

B pastes its previous clipboard content.

### Additional Information

Mouse switches trigger the fetch of announced clipboard data in `Event.PrepareToSwitchToMachine`. Hotkey switches (`MachineStuff.SwitchToMachine`) don't. Found by reading the source; not the general failure tracked in #45825.

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel 0.101.2362.0 - Stable ### Installation method PowerToys auto-update ### Area(s) with issue? File Explorer: Preview Pane ### Steps to reproduce 1. Make sure no `prevhost.exe` is running (close Explorer windows and apps that show file previews). 2. Preview a PDF in an application that hosts preview handlers at Medium integrity level. I used the preview pane of Everything 1.5a; its `prevhost.exe` runs at Medium IL. 3. Keep that preview open and select a PDF in File Explorer with the preview pane enabled. The order matters. If Explorer previews a PDF first, both previews work side by side until every preview host has exited. ### ✔️ Expected Behavior The Explorer preview pane shows the PDF, no matter whether another application previews a PDF at the same time. ### ❌ Actual Behavior The `PowerToys.PdfPreviewHandler.exe` started for Explorer dies with an unhandled .NET exception and Explorer shows no preview. Windows Error Reporting is disabled on this machine, so Windows shows the legacy dialog instead of a WER report (translated from German): > PowerToys.PdfPreviewHandler.exe - Application Error > The exception unknown software exception (0xe0434352) occurred in the application at location 0x00007FFD9D7041CA. The PdfPrevHandler log of the Explorer preview host shows `Failed to create resize event for PdfPreviewHandler` on every resize (log excerpt below). ### Additional Information Windows 11 Pro 25H2, build 26200.9457 **Two preview hosts with different integrity levels** While the crash happens, two `prevhost.exe` processes have `PowerToys.PdfPreviewHandlerCpp.dll` loaded: | Client | prevhost.exe started for | IL | Parent window of the handler exe | |---|---|---|---| | Everything | `{A5A41CC7-02CB-41D4-8C9B-9087040D6098}` (PowerToys PDF handler) | Medium | `EVERYTHING_PREVIEW_HANDLER` (Everything.exe) | | Explorer preview pane | `{914FEED8-267A-4BAA-B8AA-21E233792679}` ("Microsoft Preview Creator", shell32.dll) | Low | `Shell Preview Extension Host Previewer` (prevhost.exe) | **Root cause** Both instances use the same session-wide named event `Local\PowerToysPdfPreviewResizeEvent-5a2f162a-f728-45fe-8bda-ef3d5e434ce7`: - `PdfPreviewHandler::PdfPreviewHandler()` calls `CreateEvent(nullptr, false, false, PDF_PREVIEW_RESIZE_EVENT)` with the default security descriptor. - `PowerToys.PdfPreviewHandler.exe` opens it in `Common.UI.NativeEventWaiter.WaitForEventLoop` with `new EventWaitHandle(false, EventResetMode.AutoReset, eventName)`. That runs on a background thread without try/catch. When the Medium-IL host creates the event first, the event gets the default Medium mandatory label. The Low-IL instance is then denied access by the no-write-up policy: - C++ side: `CreateEvent` returns NULL, so the handler logs `Failed to create resize event` and continues. - .NET side: the `EventWaitHandle` constructor throws `UnauthorizedAccessException` on the background thread. The exception is unhandled and the process terminates with 0xe0434352. When the Low-IL host creates the event first, it gets a Low label and the Medium instance can open it. That is why the order matters. The event lives as long as any process holds a handle, and the C++ handler never closes `m_resizeEvent` (the destructor has no `CloseHandle`), so every preview host keeps it alive until it exits. **Verified on the affected machine** `repro-lowil-event.ps1` (below) creates the event in a Medium-IL PowerShell and opens it with an impersonated Low-IL token, the same way `NativeEventWaiter` does (output translated from German): ``` low IL: System.UnauthorizedAccessException: Access to the path 'Local\PowerToysPdfPreviewResizeEvent-test-…' is denied. control, fresh event opened at low IL: OK ``` While the Everything preview host held the real event (Medium label), opening `Local\PowerToysPdfPreviewResizeEvent-5a2f162a-…` with a Low-IL token failed the same way; a Medium token worked. No dump or stack trace is available because WER is disabled on this machine. **Still present on main** `src/common/Common.UI/NativeEventWaiter.cs` and `src/modules/previewpane/PdfPreviewHandler/Program.cs` are unchanged on `main`. `FileExplorerDllExporter/PreviewHandler.cpp` from #50252 still calls `CreateEvent(nullptr, false, false, resizeEvent)` with a global name and never closes the handle. The other preview handlers (Markdown, SVG, Monaco, G-code, Bgcode, QOI) use the same pattern and are probably affected as well. **Suggested fix** - Give each handler instance its own event name, for example by passing it to the exe as an argument. That also fixes a second problem of the shared auto-reset event: with two running instances, a resize signal wakes only one of them. - Alternatively, create the event with a security descriptor that carries a Low mandatory label (SDDL `S:(ML;;NW;;;LW)`) so Low and Medium instances can both open it. - In `NativeEventWaiter`, handle a failure to open the event instead of letting the background thread terminate the process. - Close `m_resizeEvent` in the handler's destructor. Possibly the same cause: #39851 (same dialog, closed because it could not be reproduced).

using System.Runtime.InteropServices; using System.Threading; public static class LowIlProbe { [DllImport("advapi32", SetLastError=true)] static extern bool OpenProcessToken(IntPtr h, uint a, out IntPtr t); [DllImport("advapi32", SetLastError=true)] static extern bool DuplicateTokenEx(IntPtr t, uint a, IntPtr sa, int lvl, int type, out IntPtr n); [DllImport("advapi32", SetLastError=true)] static extern bool ConvertStringSidToSid(string s, out IntPtr sid); [DllImport("advapi32", SetLastError=true)] static extern bool SetTokenInformation(IntPtr t, int c, IntPtr info, int len); [DllImport("advapi32", SetLastError=true)] static extern bool ImpersonateLoggedOnUser(IntPtr t); [DllImport("advapi32")] static extern bool RevertToSelf(); [DllImport("advapi32")] static extern int GetLengthSid(IntPtr sid); [DllImport("kernel32")] static extern IntPtr GetCurrentProcess(); // Same call as Common.UI.NativeEventWaiter.WaitForEventLoop static string Open(string name) { try { using (new EventWaitHandle(false, EventResetMode.AutoReset, name)) { return "OK"; } } catch (Exception e) { return e.GetType().FullName + ": " + e.Message; } } public static string OpenAsLowIl(string name) { IntPtr tok, dup, sid; // TOKEN_DUPLICATE | TOKEN_QUERY | TOKEN_ADJUST_DEFAULT | TOKEN_ASSIGN_PRIMARY if (!OpenProcessToken(GetCurrentProcess(), 0x2 | 0x8 | 0x80 | 0x1, out tok)) return "OpenProcessToken failed"; if (!DuplicateTokenEx(tok, 0x2000000, IntPtr.Zero, 2 /*Impersonation*/, 2 /*TokenImpersonation*/, out dup)) return "DuplicateTokenEx failed"; ConvertStringSidToSid("S-1-16-4096", out sid); // Low mandatory level IntPtr tml = Marshal.AllocHGlobal(IntPtr.Size * 2); Marshal.WriteIntPtr(tml, sid); Marshal.WriteInt32(tml, IntPtr.Size, 0x20); // SE_GROUP_INTEGRITY if (!SetTokenInformation(dup, 25 /*TokenIntegrityLevel*/, tml, IntPtr.Size * 2 + GetLengthSid(sid))) return "SetTokenInformation failed"; if (!ImpersonateLoggedOnUser(dup)) return "ImpersonateLoggedOnUser failed"; try { return Open(name); } finally { RevertToSelf(); } } } "@ $name = if ($RealName) { 'Local\PowerToysPdfPreviewResizeEvent-5a2f162a-f728-45fe-8bda-ef3d5e434ce7' } else { 'Local\PowerToysPdfPreviewResizeEvent-test-' + [guid]::NewGuid() } # 1) Medium-IL process creates the event and keeps it open (like prevhost.exe hosting the handler for a Medium-IL client) $medium = New-Object System.Threading.EventWaitHandle($false, 'AutoReset', $name) try { # 2) Low-IL code opens the same event (like PowerToys.PdfPreviewHandler.exe started by the Low-IL Explorer preview host) "event: $name" "low IL: " + [LowIlProbe]::OpenAsLowIl($name) } finally { $medium.Dispose() } # 3) Other way round: a Low-IL creator gives the event a Low label, Medium can open it $fresh = 'Local\PowerToysPdfPreviewResizeEvent-test-' + [guid]::NewGuid() "control, fresh event opened at low IL: " + [LowIlProbe]::OpenAsLowIl($fresh) ```

{"repository": "microsoft/PowerToys", "task_candidate_id": 11191, "repository_id": 165, "issue_number": 50840, "github_issue_id": 5613066550, "html_url": "https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/50840", "created_at": "2026-09-28T10:26:54+00:00", "author_association": "NONE", "title": "PDF Preview Handler crashes (0xe0434352) when Explorer previews a PDF while another app's Medium-IL preview host already uses it", "body_text": "### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel 0.101.2362.0 - Stable ### Installation method PowerToys auto-update ### Area(s) with issue? File Explorer: Preview Pane ### Steps to reproduce 1. Make sure no `prevhost.exe` is running (close Explorer windows and apps that show file previews). 2. Preview a PDF in an application that hosts preview handlers at Medium integrity level. I used the preview pane of Everything 1.5a; its `prevhost.exe` runs at Medium IL. 3. Keep that preview open and select a PDF in File Explorer with the preview pane enabled. The order matters. If Explorer previews a PDF first, both previews work side by side until every preview host has exited. ### ✔️ Expected Behavior The Explorer preview pane shows the PDF, no matter whether another application previews a PDF at the same time. ### ❌ Actual Behavior The `PowerToys.PdfPreviewHandler.exe` started for Explorer dies with an unhandled .NET exception and Explorer shows no preview. Windows Error Reporting is disabled on this machine, so Windows shows the legacy dialog instead of a WER report (translated from German): > PowerToys.PdfPreviewHandler.exe - Application Error > The exception unknown software exception (0xe0434352) occurred in the application at location 0x00007FFD9D7041CA. The PdfPrevHandler log of the Explorer preview host shows `Failed to create resize event for PdfPreviewHandler` on every resize (log excerpt below). ### Additional Information Windows 11 Pro 25H2, build 26200.9457 **Two preview hosts with different integrity levels** While the crash happens, two `prevhost.exe` processes have `PowerToys.PdfPreviewHandlerCpp.dll` loaded: | Client | prevhost.exe started for | IL | Parent window of the handler exe | |---|---|---|---| | Everything | `{A5A41CC7-02CB-41D4-8C9B-9087040D6098}` (PowerToys PDF handler) | Medium | `EVERYTHING_PREVIEW_HANDLER` (Everything.exe) | | Explorer preview pane | `{914FEED8-267A-4BAA-B8AA-21E233792679}` ("Microsoft Preview Creator", shell32.dll) | Low | `Shell Preview Extension Host Previewer` (prevhost.exe) | **Root cause** Both instances use the same session-wide named event `Local\PowerToysPdfPreviewResizeEvent-5a2f162a-f728-45fe-8bda-ef3d5e434ce7`: - `PdfPreviewHandler::PdfPreviewHandler()` calls `CreateEvent(nullptr, false, false, PDF_PREVIEW_RESIZE_EVENT)` with the default security descriptor. - `PowerToys.PdfPreviewHandler.exe` opens it in `Common.UI.NativeEventWaiter.WaitForEventLoop` with `new EventWaitHandle(false, EventResetMode.AutoReset, eventName)`. That runs on a background thread without try/catch. When the Medium-IL host creates the event first, the event gets the default Medium mandatory label. The Low-IL instance is then denied access by the no-write-up policy: - C++ side: `CreateEvent` returns NULL, so the handler logs `Failed to create resize event` and continues. - .NET side: the `EventWaitHandle` constructor throws `UnauthorizedAccessException` on the background thread. The exception is unhandled and the process terminates with 0xe0434352. When the Low-IL host creates the event first, it gets a Low label and the Medium instance can open it. That is why the order matters. The event lives as long as any process holds a handle, and the C++ handler never closes `m_resizeEvent` (the destructor has no `CloseHandle`), so every preview host keeps it alive until it exits. **Verified on the affected machine** `repro-lowil-event.ps1` (below) creates the event in a Medium-IL PowerShell and opens it with an impersonated Low-IL token, the same way `NativeEventWaiter` does (output translated from German): ``` low IL: System.UnauthorizedAccessException: Access to the path 'Local\PowerToysPdfPreviewResizeEvent-test-…' is denied. control, fresh event opened at low IL: OK ``` While the Everything preview host held the real event (Medium label), opening `Local\PowerToysPdfPreviewResizeEvent-5a2f162a-…` with a Low-IL token failed the same way; a Medium token worked. No dump or stack trace is available because WER is disabled on this machine. **Still present on main** `src/common/Common.UI/NativeEventWaiter.cs` and `src/modules/previewpane/PdfPreviewHandler/Program.cs` are unchanged on `main`. `FileExplorerDllExporter/PreviewHandler.cpp` from #50252 still calls `CreateEvent(nullptr, false, false, resizeEvent)` with a global name and never closes the handle. The other preview handlers (Markdown, SVG, Monaco, G-code, Bgcode, QOI) use the same pattern and are probably affected as well. **Suggested fix** - Give each handler instance its own event name, for example by passing it to the exe as an argument. That also fixes a second problem of the shared auto-reset event: with two running instances, a resize signal wakes only one of them. - Alternatively, create the event with a security descriptor that carries a Low mandatory label (SDDL `S:(ML;;NW;;;LW)`) so Low and Medium instances can both open it. - In `NativeEventWaiter`, handle a failure to open the event instead of letting the background thread terminate the process. - Close `m_resizeEvent` in the handler's destructor. Possibly the same cause: #39851 (same dialog, closed because it could not be reproduced).

Mouse Utilities ### Steps to reproduce The Mouse Pointer Crosshairs utility becomes unresponsive and locks its position when clicking inside the client area of an active application window. Once locked, the crosshair does not follow the mouse until the user clicks directly on the desktop, which temporarily restores functionality until another application window is clicked. ### ✔️ Expected Behavior The mouse pointer crosshairs should remain active and smoothly follow the mouse cursor regardless of whether the cursor is over the desktop or an application window. ### ❌ Actual Behavior The crosshairs freeze in place at the exact spot where the application window was clicked. ### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Add an option to Light Switch such that when Light Switch enables/disables dark mode, it will also:

1. Enable/Disable Edge's "Auto Dark Mode for Web Contents" (enable-force-dark) Experiments flag when Light Switch enables/disables dark mode
2. Ask the user if it is OK to restart Edge in order for the enable-force-dark flag to take effect

### Scenario when this would be used?

When a user wants to 

1. view web pages that do not automatically switch to dark mode when the Edge browser itself is configured to use dark mode, but 
2. wants pages to resume being displayed in light mode when Edge is configured to light mode

For example, learn.microsoft.com continues to display pages in light mode even when Edge itself is configured to use dark mode. If the user manually uses the enable-force-dark flag, learn.microsoft.com will display pages in dark mode, even when Edge itself is configured to use light mode.
