body_text: ### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel 0.102 (current main) ### Installation method Dev build in Visual Studio ### Area(s) with issue? Shortcut Guide ### Steps to reproduce Run PowerToys with Shortcut Guide enabled. ### ✔️ Expected Behavior The Windows taskbar remains at the top of the z-order. Dragging windows across a taskbar does not obscure it. ### ❌ Actual Behavior The taskbar is obscured by the window: If the user has the option to show the taskbar on every display, this occurs for all taskbars. Each taskbar still has its `WS_EX_TOPMOST` extended style bit set, but their shell z-order ranking gets demoted relative to application windows. This seems unique to Shortcut Guide. Running it independent of Runner exhibits the issue. ### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file _No response_ ### Additional Information I thought this was because Windows was regarding the overlay as an exclusive full-screen "rude" window (e.g. a full-screen game), so the taskbar is moved back in the shell z-order. However, setting the `OverlayWindow`'s HWND to `NonRudeHWND` via a `SetPropW` call did not change the behaviour. ### Other Software _No response_

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

# [Feature Request] Customizable Windows Profiles

## Description

It would be great if PowerToys could provide a **Windows Customization Profiles** feature that allows users to save and quickly switch between different Windows setups.

For example, a user could create profiles such as:

### 💻 Coding

* Dark/light theme
* Wallpaper
* Accent color
* Preferred window layout
* Selected applications
* Monitor arrangement

### 🎮 Gaming

* Gaming wallpaper
* Dark theme
* Gaming-related applications

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

There is a strong need for new image formats suitable for the web and modern browsers: WEBP (with settings) and APNG.
1. Additional useful feature (checkbox):
    It would be desirable to add a "maximum compression" checkbox to the settings for each image type, similar to TinyPNG.
2. Additional useful feature (checkbox):
    It would be desirable to add a "maximum compression" checkbox to the settings for each image type that appends the suffix "_opti" to the end of the filename.
2. Additional useful feature (Drop-down list):
    Automatic image cropping for standard social media image sizes (Facebook, Instagram). Not as critical as the previous features, but it adds to the ease of use.

P.S. Thank you very much for this useful plugin.

### Scenario when this would be used?

For webmasters, copywriters, bloggers, and creators of content for websites and social media. This plugin can make the internet faster and reduce server load and traffic :)

### Supporting information

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.100.2

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

Power Display

### Steps to reproduce

Primary monitor connected over HDMI to Dedicated NVIDIA GPU, secondary monitor connected over CPU onboard HDMI port. Enable power display, accept the warnings. Scan for monitors. Display config set to hybrid so as to enable both radeon iGPU and dedicated nvidia GPU.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Should detect both the monitors, and the primary monitor being pretty much modern, launched within under last 5 years, it should be more compatible and reliable. (AOC 34 ultrawide office monitor (non gaming) ) and the secondary monitor is any ways legacy vga monitor (at least 15 years old) connected hdmi to vga converter.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The Secondary monitor detects fine, controls work fine. And the primary monitor (newer more recent one) doesnt detect at all, with no option to delete cache/restart the scan from begining. (I wish there was an option to delete whatever this sub application - Power Display had config and start fresh, so that i could have tested it only connecting primary monitor, then eventually second monitor

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

OS Version: Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 
.NET Version: .NET 10.0.9
PowerToys is running as user (non-elevated)
Install scope: per user
Operating System Language: English (India)
System locale: en-IN

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.100.2

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

Advanced Paste

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an OpenAI model provider in Advanced Paste → Paste with AI using model gpt-6-luna and a valid OpenAI API key.
2. Leave Advanced AI – Use built-in functions to handle complex tasks disabled.
3. Use Paste with AI. The model works normally.
4. Enable Advanced AI for the same model.
5. Copy some text, open Advanced Paste and make a Paste with AI request.
6. The request fails with OpenAI request failed with status code: 400.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Advanced AI should work with an OpenAI model that supports function tools, or PowerToys should configure the request appropriately for the selected model/API.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

With Advanced AI enabled, OpenAI rejects the request:

> Microsoft.SemanticKernel.HttpOperationException: HTTP 400 (invalid_request_error: )
> Parameter: reasoning_effort
> 
> Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported for gpt-6-luna in /v1/chat/completions. To use function tools, use /v1/responses or set reasoning_effort to 'none'.

The same gpt-6-luna provider works when Advanced AI is disabled.

### Cause

The Advanced AI path enables automatic Semantic Kernel function calling:

[https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.100.2/src/modules/AdvancedPaste/AdvancedPaste/Services/AdvancedAIKernelService.cs](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.100.2/src/modules/AdvancedPaste/AdvancedPaste/Services/AdvancedAIKernelService.cs)

```
return new OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings
{
    FunctionChoiceBehavior = FunctionChoiceBehavior.Auto(),
};
```

The provider is registered with AddOpenAIChatCompletion, so this uses OpenAI's /v1/chat/completions API.

Enabling Advanced AI therefore adds PowerToys' built-in actions as function tools. For gpt-6-luna, the Chat Completions API rejects function tools when reasoning is enabled/defaulted and requires either:

- reasoning_effort: "none"; or
- use of the /v1/responses API.

This also appears to remain applicable to the current main implementation, which still uses AddOpenAIChatCompletion and FunctionChoiceBehavior.Auto() for the Advanced AI path.

### Possible short-term fix

For models that require reasoning to be disabled when combining Chat Completions with function tools, explicitly send:

  "reasoning_effort": "none"

PowerToys currently references OpenAI .NET SDK 2.7.0. Although Semantic Kernel 1.71.0's string conversion only recognises low, medium, high and minimal, the underlying OpenAI SDK exposes a public ChatReasoningEffortLevel(string value) constructor, and Semantic Kernel accepts a ChatReasoningEffortLevel instance directly.

For example, a model-specific proof of concept is:

```
using OpenAI.Chat;

#pragma warning disable OPENAI001
return new OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings
{
    FunctionChoiceBehavior = FunctionChoiceBehavior.Auto(),
    ReasoningEffort =
        string.Equals(
            runtimeConfig.ModelName,
            "gpt-6-luna",
            StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        ? new ChatReasoningEffortLevel("none")
        : null,
};
#pragma warning restore OPENAI001
```
I would not suggest applying reasoning_effort: "none" unconditionally, because models that do not support the parameter may themselves return HTTP 400.

A more general capability-based implementation would avoid hardcoding individual models.

### Longer-term fix

For newer reasoning models, using OpenAI's Responses API for the Advanced AI/tool-calling path may be preferable. The API error explicitly recommends /v1/responses when combining function tools with reasoning.

That would allow Advanced AI to retain reasoning rather than disabling it solely to remain compatible with /v1/chat/completions.

### Related issue

This is related in nature to #49838, but appears to be a different problem:

#49838 concerned PowerToys explicitly setting an incompatible reasoning_effort value for ordinary custom actions. In this case PowerToys does not explicitly set ReasoningEffort; the failure occurs specifically when Advanced AI enables function tools for gpt-6-luna through /v1/chat/completions.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

We need a tool that auto-clicks the notification toasts ("notification banners").

Ideally should be able to filter by the toast's caption title (the name of the toast's originator as it appears under "Notifications from apps and other senders" in Settings/Notifications) and the button text, with two or three button texts to click ,in order of preferences, e.g. if a button matches "Text1" then click it, else if a button matches "Text2" then click it, else if a button matches "Text3" then click it.

The understanding is that clicking the button closes/acknowledges the notification by clicking the preferred button. If the button text on the banner does not match any of the ordered presets, do nothing. Extra credits if this works for notifications not shown as banner but in the notification Center only (if that is still a thing)

Obviously the new PowerToy should be based on some sort of hook and not just watch the screen or click blindly, and can also read the button's text in a deterministic manner. Hopefully a [notification listener ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/app-notifications/notification-listener) can do that?

### Scenario when this would be used?

This would help with Very Long (days) running processes that ask the user random questions through toast notifications at random times.

body_text:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Perhaps a toggle to enable, but dragging a window's title bar with the right mouse button begins the existing window drag feature (without a modifier key, and without changing window focus). Acorn's RISC OS had this feature which I always thought was nice and is something I've always missed in Windows.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Most of the same scenarios as the existing power toy. You do have to be able to see the title bar to do this, but it saves using the modifier key making it slightly more accessible and intuitive.

### Supporting information

Essentially, I think it could be a really useful feature as it provides the ability to use the Grab and Move without the modifier key, and I don't think right-dragging a title bar would interfere with any other operation. I've vibe-coded a very simple tray application that does just this function and it works great, but then I found Grab and Move and it's better implementation, simply lacking the right-drag option which I think people would benefit from (and an option).

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0 - Preview

### Installation method

Microsoft Store

### Area(s) with issue?

Keyboard Manager

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open **PowerToys Settings** and navigate to **Keyboard Manager**.
2. Click on **Remap a shortcut**.
3. Add a rule to disable a shortcut:
   - **Shortcut:** `Win + Ctrl + D`
   - **Mapped to:** `Disable`
4. Test pressing `Win + Ctrl + D` alone -> The shortcut is successfully disabled (no virtual desktop is created).
5. Now, press and hold `Win + Ctrl + S` and simultaneously press `D` (or press `Win + Ctrl + S + D` at once, which frequently happens during gaming when moving with WASD while crouching with Ctrl).

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

`Win + Ctrl + D` should remain disabled/suppressed according to the remap rule. Holding down additional keys (such as `S` for movement) should not bypass the shortcut matcher or leak underlying native Windows shortcuts.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The remapping / disabling rule for `Win + Ctrl + D` is completely bypassed.
Windows receives and triggers both system shortcuts simultaneously:
- `Win + Ctrl + S` is fired (e.g., Windows Speech Recognition opens).
- `Win + Ctrl + D` is fired (e.g., a new Virtual Desktop is created).
Both combinations leak through to the OS during multi-key rollover.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

It would be helpful to be able to select a predetermined display profile with a quick shortcut—whether with a unique shortcut for each profile or with just one shortcut to cycle through profiles and stop at a desired one. This is separate logic from having shortcuts to change different settings for each display (existing issue). As I understand it, it's a more complex task with many variables. But switching profiles doesn't directly connect shortcuts to display settings—just to different menu items in the flyout. Presumably, profile shortcuts could be implemented faster and more easily than display settings shortcuts. Also, when selecting a profile with a shortcut, it's worth popping up the flyout and having the newly selected profile name visible—to know which profile was selected. 

P.S. Visibility of a selected profile name near the profile select menu icon in the flyout has a separate issue ( #50864 ).

### Scenario when this would be used?

I have two displays and 5 different profiles depending on the time of day and light conditions. Each time, I have to do many clicks or key presses to get to the profile-changing menu. It'd be helpful to have something simpler, like one shortcut to switch profiles.

It would be helpful to be able to select a predetermined display profile with a quick shortcut—whether with a unique shortcut for each profile or with just one shortcut to cycle through profiles and stop at a desired one. This is separate logic from having shortcuts to change different settings for each display (existing issue). As I understand it, it's a more complex task with many variables. But switching profiles doesn't directly connect shortcuts to display settings—just to different menu items in the flyout. Presumably, profile shortcuts could be implemented faster and more easily than display settings shortcuts. Also, when selecting a profile with a shortcut, it's worth popping up the flyout and having the newly selected profile name visible—to know which profile was selected. 

P.S. Visibility of a selected profile name near the profile select menu icon in the flyout has a separate issue ( #50864 ).

### Scenario when this would be used?

I have two displays and 5 different profiles depending on the time of day and light conditions. Each time, I have to do many clicks or key presses to get to the profile-changing menu. It'd be helpful to have something simpler, like one shortcut to switch profiles.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I would like to add CPU package/core temperature to Command Palette's Performance Monitor after the GPU temperature work in #50915. Before starting that implementation, I would like to discuss whether the required driver or SDK dependencies would be acceptable for PowerToys.

The GPU implementation uses Windows' D3DKMT/WDDM interface and does not require an additional vendor driver or SDK. CPU package/core temperature needs a different approach: I expect it to require vendor-specific hardware access and a supporting driver or SDK dependency. For example, [Intel PCM uses an MSR kernel driver on Windows](https://github.com/intel/pcm/blob/master/doc/WINDOWS_HOWTO.md).

Would a vendor-specific driver or SDK dependency be acceptable for a separate CPU temperature implementation? If so, is there a preferred approach or existing dependency I should use, and any requirements around driver distribution, signing, or administrator privileges?

I have not selected a dependency yet. I would appreciate maintainer guidance here before proceeding with that work.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Users could check CPU package/core temperature alongside the existing performance metrics while running CPU-intensive workloads.

This should report an actual CPU sensor reading. ACPI thermal-zone readings cannot reliably be presented as CPU temperature, as discussed in the review of #48639.

### Supporting information

- #46434 tracks the broader request for temperature readings.
- #48639 attempted an ACPI thermal-zone implementation and was closed without merging.
- #50915 implements GPU temperature through D3DKMT.

This issue is specifically for the CPU implementation and dependency discussion. Please continue that discussion here so the GPU PR can remain focused on its existing scope.

body_text:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Workspaces can already start a group of apps with saved position, size, window state (e.g. maximized), CLI arguments and admin rights. What is missing is a way to start a workspace automatically at Windows sign-in, with a start delay.

Proposal:

1. A per-workspace option "Launch at sign-in" (e.g. next to "Create desktop shortcut" / "Move existing windows").
2. A configurable start delay, either per workspace (e.g. 0 s, 30 s, 1 min, 5 min) or, ideally, per app within the workspace, so that apps start staggered instead of all at once.
3. Optional: an option to start the apps one after another with a fixed interval.

The existing per-app data model (position, state, arguments) would only need one additional field, "delay".

### Scenario when this would be used?

After sign-in, many programs (cloud sync, mail client, messengers, backup tools, CAD/slicer software, music player) start at the same time and compete for disk, CPU and network. The system stays sluggish for minutes, and windows end up in random places.

With Workspaces I can already define where each app should be placed and in which state. But I still have to start the workspace manually after every login. Windows itself offers no good alternative:

- Settings > Apps > Startup and shell:startup only allow enabling/disabling, there is no per-app delay.
- The "Run: minimized/maximized" setting of a shortcut is ignored by many apps.
- The only workaround is a Task Scheduler task (trigger "At log on" + "Delay task for") that launches the Workspaces desktop shortcut. That works, but it is a manual, fragile setup outside of PowerToys and has to be maintained separately for every workspace.

Built-in autostart with delay would make Workspaces a complete replacement for startup scripts: the desktop is usable right after login, the load is spread out, and every app ends up where it belongs.

### Supporting information

Current workaround: create the desktop shortcut for the workspace, then use Task Scheduler (taskschd.msc) with trigger "At log on" and "Delay task for" (advanced settings), action = start the shortcut.

Third-party tools such as Startup Delayer offer per-app delays, but they know nothing about Workspaces layouts.

body_text: ### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel 0.101.2362.0 — Stable; new WinUI 3 editor enabled (useNewEditor: true) ### Installation method GitHub — installed from [GitHub release v0.101.2362.0](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/releases/tag/v0.101.2362.0). ### Area(s) with issue? Keyboard Manager ### Steps to reproduce Installation details: machine-wide installation under C:\Program Files\PowerToys; installed from the GitHub release linked above. An existing configuration has three mappings with the trigger Ctrl (Left) + Shift (Left) + N (162;160;78): | Scope | Action | | --- | --- | | Global | Open Chrome | | code.exe | Remap to Ctrl (Left) + Shift (Right) + N | | parsecd.exe | Remap to Ctrl (Left) + Shift (Right) + N | 1. Open this existing configuration in the new Keyboard Manager editor. 2. Edit the global Open app mapping. 3. Keep the trigger unchanged and leave Only apply to a specific app unchecked. 4. Observe the Duplicate remapping validation error. The observed screenshot shows the error in Edit remapping, with Allow chords checked. This configuration previously worked; the exact last working version is unknown. Suggested minimal reproduction: one global shortcut mapping and one app-specific override of the same trigger, then edit the global mapping. This reduced two-entry case has not been tested separately. ### ✔️ Expected Behavior Allow a global shortcut mapping and app-specific overrides with the same trigger. In a matching app, the app-specific mapping should take precedence; elsewhere, the global mapping should apply. This behavior is described in the [Keyboard Manager engine documentation](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/doc/devdocs/modules/keyboardmanager/keyboardmanager.md): app-specific shortcut handling runs before global shortcut handling so the app-specific variant takes precedence. ### ❌ Actual Behavior The editor displays: > Duplicate remapping — This key or shortcut is already remapped. There is exactly one mapping per scope for this trigger. Both default.json and editorSettings.json confirm these distinct scopes; all three editor entries are active. ### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file _No response_ ### Additional Information Windows 11 Home, 26H2, build 26300.9550, 64-bit. Machine-wide installation under C:\Program Files\PowerToys; installed from GitHub release v0.101.2362.0. Evidence: user-supplied screenshot and read-only inspection of the current configuration. No mappings were changed during investigation. No separate runtime test or preview-version test was performed. **Likely cause:** [ValidationHelper.IsDuplicateMapping in v0.101.2362.0](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.101.2362.0/src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Helpers/ValidationHelper.cs#L202-L209) uses this app-scope predicate: ```csharp string.IsNullOrEmpty(settings.Shortcut.TargetApp) || string.IsNullOrEmpty(appName) || settings.Shortcut.TargetApp == appName ``` When editing a global mapping, appName is empty, so matching triggers from every app scope count as duplicates. Here, the count is three and exceeds the edit-mode tolerance of one. **Existing reports and fixes checked:** #48749 concerns entries being duplicated on save, rather than this global/app-scope false positive. #49710 was closed by merged PR #50265, which changes edit-mode identity exclusion and filters inactive entries. However, [the current main-branch implementation](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Helpers/ValidationHelper.cs#L209-L225) still has the same empty-app OR predicate. That related fix does not address this scope comparison. Suggested correction: compare normalized application scopes for duplicate detection, preserving global mappings and app-specific overrides as distinct while rejecting duplicate triggers within the same scope. Relevant configuration excerpt (optional launch arguments omitted): ```json { "remapShortcuts": { "global": [{ "originalKeys": "162;160;78", "exactMatch": false, "operationType": 1, "runProgramFilePath": "C:\\Program Files\\Google\\Chrome\\Application\\chrome.exe" }], "appSpecific": [ { "originalKeys": "162;160;78", "newRemapKeys": "162;161;78", "exactMatch": false, "operationType": 0, "targetApp": "code.exe" }, { "originalKeys": "162;160;78", "newRemapKeys": "162;161;78", "exactMatch": false, "operationType": 0, "targetApp": "parsecd.exe" } ] } } ``` ### Other Software Google Chrome, Visual Studio Code (code.exe), and Parsec (parsecd.exe). Their versions were not collected; the observed failure is editor validation. ### Screenshot

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0 — Stable; new WinUI 3 editor enabled (useNewEditor: true). Restored backup manifest: v0.100.2.

### Installation method

GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

Keyboard Manager, Settings

### Steps to reproduce

Installation details: machine-wide installation under `C:\Program Files\PowerToys`, installed from [GitHub release v0.101.2362.0](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/releases/tag/v0.101.2362.0). Version/channel and installation details match my existing report #50933.

**Observed restore scenario:**

1. The destination PC already has a new Keyboard Manager editor configuration in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\PowerToys\Keyboard Manager\editorSettings.json`, with `useNewEditor: true`.
2. Restore a PowerToys backup whose global Open app shortcut has different Chrome arguments and launch options from that existing editor configuration.
3. PowerToys restores `Keyboard Manager\default.json` and restarts.
4. Compare the restored runtime shortcut with the same global shortcut in `editorSettings.json`.

For the global left Ctrl + left Shift + N shortcut, the observed post-restore values were:

| Setting | Restored runtime `default.json` | Existing `editorSettings.json` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chrome arguments | `--profile-directory="Profile Local" https://www.google.com/` | `--profile-directory="LocalProfile" https://www.google.com/` |
| Already running | `runProgramAlreadyRunningAction: 1` (Start another) | `IfRunningAction: 0` (Show window) |
| Window visibility | `runProgramStartWindowType: 3` (Maximized) | `Visibility: 0` (Normal) |

The restore log specifically records `Keyboard Manager\default.json` being updated from backup. The Keyboard Manager engine subsequently logged launching Chrome with the restored `Profile Local` arguments, confirming that the **runtime restore succeeded**.

The extracted backup manifest lists `default.json` but does not list `editorSettings.json`. The existing editor file retained its older save timestamp and values.

**Deterministic filter test, run separately without changing live settings:**

The installed `WinUI3Apps\backup_restore_settings.json` includes `*Keyboard Manager\default.json` and generic `*settings.json`, but no explicit pattern for `editorSettings.json`.

This PowerShell test uses the same wildcard-to-regex conversion as the backup implementation:

```powershell
$path = 'C:\Example\Microsoft\PowerToys\Keyboard Manager\editorSettings.json'
$regex = '^' + [regex]::Escape('*settings.json').Replace('\*', '.*') + '$'
[regex]::IsMatch($path, $regex) # False
[regex]::IsMatch($path, $regex, [System.Text.RegularExpressions.RegexOptions]::IgnoreCase) # True
```

Testing that path against **every installed include pattern** also returned no match.

The actual restore and saved-file mismatch were inspected. A separate clean-install UI reproduction and a save-from-stale-editor overwrite test were not performed.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

After restoring a backup, the new Keyboard Manager editor should agree with the restored runtime mappings and launch options.

Backup/restore should either preserve the required new editor state or reliably reconcile existing editor state with the restored runtime configuration.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The runtime settings restore successfully, while the separate persisted new editor settings remain stale. This leaves two conflicting saved representations of the same shortcut and creates a risk that a subsequent editor save could restore old values. That overwrite risk has not been tested in this report.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[PowerToys-KeyboardManager-backup-sanitized-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32935374/PowerToys-KeyboardManager-backup-sanitized-evidence.zip)

### Additional Information

- Windows 11 Home, 26H2, OS build **26300.9550**, 64-bit.
- New editor enabled: `useNewEditor: true`.
- Inspection and filter test performed October 1, 2026.
- Workaround used: with editors closed, back up both files and correct only the affected shortcut's arguments and launch options in both saved representations. Unrelated mappings were preserved.
- Attached a focused, sanitized evidence ZIP containing the pre-fix affected-shortcut fields, relevant official-report log excerpts, and installed backup include filters. This is not the complete unmodified bug-report ZIP. The official report was generated after the workaround; pre-fix values come from preserved originals. Unrelated settings, personal paths, and system inventories were omitted.

**Likely cause:**

1. [Backup include rules in v0.101.2362.0](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.101.2362.0/src/settings-ui/Settings.UI.Library/backup_restore_settings.json) omit an explicit `editorSettings.json` pattern. The same rules are present in v0.100.2.
2. [IsIncludeFile / GetSettingsFiles](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.101.2362.0/src/settings-ui/Settings.UI.Library/SettingsBackupAndRestoreUtils.cs#L526-L567) use `Regex.IsMatch` without `IgnoreCase`. The capital **S** in `editorSettings.json` therefore prevents a match with lowercase `*settings.json`.
3. [SettingsManager.LoadSettings in the installed release](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.101.2362.0/src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Settings/SettingsManager.cs#L50-L75) imports native mappings when the editor file does not exist, but reads the existing editor file when it is present.

The filter omission is reproduced directly; the explanation of how it causes the stale editor state follows from the inspected files and release source.

Please consider explicitly including the editor file with suitable restore semantics, and/or reconciling editor state after a runtime configuration restore. Merely creating another standard backup still excludes the editor file under these rules.

### Other Software

Google Chrome (used for the Open app shortcut).

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[PowerToys-KeyboardManager-backup-sanitized-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32935374/PowerToys-KeyboardManager-backup-sanitized-evidence.zip)

### Additional Information

- Windows 11 Home, 26H2, OS build **26300.9550**, 64-bit.
- New editor enabled: `useNewEditor: true`.
- Inspection and filter test performed October 1, 2026.
- Workaround used: with editors closed, back up both files and correct only the affected shortcut's arguments and launch options in both saved representations. Unrelated mappings were preserved.
- Attached a focused, sanitized evidence ZIP containing the pre-fix affected-shortcut fields, relevant official-report log excerpts, and installed backup include filters. This is not the complete unmodified bug-report ZIP. The official report was generated after the workaround; pre-fix values come from preserved originals. Unrelated settings, personal paths, and system inventories were omitted.

**Likely cause:**

1. [Backup include rules in v0.101.2362.0](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.101.2362.0/src/settings-ui/Settings.UI.Library/backup_restore_settings.json) omit an explicit `editorSettings.json` pattern. The same rules are present in v0.100.2.
2. [IsIncludeFile / GetSettingsFiles](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.101.2362.0/src/settings-ui/Settings.UI.Library/SettingsBackupAndRestoreUtils.cs#L526-L567) use `Regex.IsMatch` without `IgnoreCase`. The capital **S** in `editorSettings.json` therefore prevents a match with lowercase `*settings.json`.
3. [SettingsManager.LoadSettings in the installed release](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.101.2362.0/src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Settings/SettingsManager.cs#L50-L75) imports native mappings when the editor file does not exist, but reads the existing editor file when it is present.

The filter omission is reproduced directly; the explanation of how it causes the stale editor state follows from the inspected files and release source.

Please consider explicitly including the editor file with suitable restore semantics, and/or reconciling editor state after a runtime configuration restore. Merely creating another standard backup still excludes the editor file under these rules.

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.100.2

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

Power Display

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start **Power Display** on the physical system and leave it running.
2. From another device, connect to the system using **Remote Desktop**.
3. Complete any work in the Remote Desktop session.
4. Disconnect/exit the Remote Desktop session.
5. Return to the physical system and log in.
6. Open **Power Display** and attempt to adjust the monitor/display parameters.
7. Observe that **no connected monitors are detected**.
8. Click **Rescan Connected**.
9. Observe that the connected monitors are detected again and become available for configuration.



### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Connected monitors should remain detected by Power Display after an RDP session ends, without requiring a manual rescan.


### ❌ Actual Behavior

After returning from an RDP session, Power Display reports that no monitors are detected until **Rescan Connected** is manually triggered.


### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

This behavior was not observed with **Monitorian**, as far as I recall.

body_text:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

The proposed functionality uses the behavior of the software "Groupy 2" as a reference, which allows users to drag and group Windows applications into tabs within a single main container. However, PowerToys would expand upon this by adding a fundamental feature that Groupy 2 lacks: the ability to split the viewing area within that same grouped window. Users could grab a tab and snap it side-by-side with another tab inside the same container. The expected behavior is that the main window controls (minimize, maximize, restore, and move) would affect the entire group simultaneously. If two windows are split side-by-side within this group, clicking "minimize" would collapse both with a single click.

### Scenario when this would be used?

For power users, managing individual windows requires excessive clicking and disrupts productivity. A practical use case is for day traders managing multiple accounts, who need to keep two or more instances of trading platforms (like Profit or MetaTrader) open side-by-side. Currently, Windows forces users to minimize each instance independently. With this feature, they could group the terminals into a single window (like Groupy 2), split them side-by-side for simultaneous viewing, and minimize them all as a single application to quickly clear the desktop. This naturally applies to many other scenarios, such as grouping multiple spreadsheet files into tabs and easily switching between them.

(https://1drv.ms/v/c/fd0b5146bb1c804b/IQBCpba7bJWBRpTH3acv2o8_AfOIudUJlDBQSdNOjzz8w0o?e=mZ5aEa)

(Note: I tried to attach a video demonstrating this, but the upload failed.)

### Supporting information

The primary usability reference for the tab system is Stardock's "Groupy 2," which proves the immense utility of grouping applications in Windows but falls short by not allowing two tabs to be viewed simultaneously. The reference for the internal split-view is the Microsoft Edge browser, which introduced a native "Split screen" feature for viewing two pages side-by-side within the same window. Combining Groupy 2's tab mechanics with Edge's split-screen capabilities at the OS level would be an indispensable productivity innovation for Windows.

body_text:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.111.2

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

Run a Full Screen Windowed (Not Full Screen Exclusive) application and the mouse won't move between devices.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Until today when I am playing a Full Screen Windowed game on my primary PC I was able to move my mouse pointer to the secondary PC and then sue that PC like a second screen with full mouse and keyboard input from the primary PC.  I have been using Mouse Without Boarders like this for many years now.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

When the Full screen Windowed application is in focus I cannot move my mouse to the screen of the secondary PC.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[PowerToysReport_2026-10-02-20-22-56.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32988134/PowerToysReport_2026-10-02-20-22-56.zip)

### Additional Information

Windows 11 Pro


### Other Software

Final Fantasy XIV
Star Trek Online

### __Description of the new feature / enhancement__

While the new **Window Hopper** tool is great, I really wouldn't mind having the opposite of it as well: an **App Hopper**.

Pressing a shortcut would make you **switch focus from the currently-active program to the other programs**, sorted by most recently active. It would work like alt-tab or Window Hopper when the shortcut is pressed. 

If the hopped-to program had several windows then it would default to focusing on the most recently-used window.

### Scenario when this would be used?

When I'm switching between several browser windows and now suddenly want to go to Discord without having to press alt-tab 5 times. But there can be MANY use case scenarios.

### Supporting information

Maybe it could be called the Program Hopper. 

Importantly, this **shouldn't be a new PowerToy** but both the Window Hopper and this App Hopper should be **combined into one single "Hopper" PowerToy**. There you could set all the settings for both Window Hopper and for App Hopper, **including** setting each of them on/off independently. 

There should be an off-by-default option to only show program icons and not previews of the window that will be selected when you're App Hopping.

body_text:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

While resizing a window by one of its edges (or a corner), snap the dragged edge to the nearest zone boundary of the active FancyZones layout when the mouse button is released. Only the edge being dragged moves. The other edges stay where they are. No other windows or zones are resized.

Original request https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/9146 incorrectly marked as duplicate.

This is **not** asking for:

- any other windows be resized
- any zones be resized or modified
- snapping to other windows
- snapping to to screen edges

Existing unrelated issues:

- https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/254
- https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/8

### Scenario when this would be used?

Manually resizing windows

### Supporting information

Original request and discussion: 

- #9146

The interaction described above was clarified in that thread, including feidaman's comment that only the dragged border should snap and that the nearest boundary line should be highlighted.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

The Keyboard Manager is missing a great opportunity by not supporting mouse actions alongside keyboard keypresses. E.g., when I press "V" on my keyboard with my left hand and rotate my mouse wheel with my right hand, it could be mapped to change the sound volume. This would open a plethora of new opportunities.

### Scenario when this would be used?

The combo keyboard keypress + mouse wheel or key action could be mapped to anything the Keyboard Manager already maps to. E.g., a keyboard shortcut + mouse left-click could launch an application, etc.

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362 stable

### Installation method

WinGet

### Area(s) with issue?

General

### Steps to reproduce

I don't know how to describe the reproduction well, but my setup is the following:

- Enabled: Find My Mouse, Colour Picker, Screen Ruler, Shortcut Guide, Always On Top, File Explorer Addons, File Locksmith
- Crucially **disabled**: Awake, Command Palette, Mouse Highlighter
- Rest of modules are disabled as well unless they've been added since I last went through all of them some versions back

Every single time I logout of my user account and/or (re)start my system, the three modules highlighted above as absolutely **disabled** show up again. I don't know 100% that it's _just_ those three but those three are extremely noticeable (Awake and Command Palette have tray icons & Mouse Highlighter is very annoying with its yellow circles on *every click*).

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Modules I disabled stay disabled

### ❌ Actual Behavior

At least Awake, Command Palette, and Mouse Highlighter re-enable themselves forcibly on every relog/restart.

There may be more modules exhibiting this behaviour but those aren't as intrusively obviously enabled.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[PowerToysReport_2026-10-05-12-20-28.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33053464/PowerToysReport_2026-10-05-12-20-28.zip)

### Additional Information

- Windows 11 Pro 26H2
- System Language: German, PowerToys language: English
- User installation
- Running as user (shown in General settings)

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

Current Command Palette development build (observed October 5, 2026)

### Installation method

Dev build in Visual Studio

### Area(s) with issue?

Command Palette

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable the Command Palette Taskbar Dock on the local desktop.
2. Open a Windows Dev Box session.
3. Maximize the Dev Box window.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The maximized Dev Box window should respect the Dock work area, so the Dock does not cover the remote desktop content.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The local Command Palette Dock renders on top of the maximized Dev Box window and covers part of its content.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

The Dock is running on the physical/local desktop; the maximized window contains the Dev Box desktop.

### Other Software

Windows Dev Box client

Command Palette

The Dock temporarily renders with an incorrect layout after switching from left to bottom. It returns to the correct appearance after a few seconds.

_No response_

### Additional Information

The incorrect state is transient but clearly visible during the position change.

Current Command Palette development build (observed October 5, 2026)

Dev build in Visual Studio

### Area(s) with issue?

Command Palette

body_text: ### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel 0.101.2362 stable ### Installation method WinGet ### Area(s) with issue? FancyZones ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run PowerToys as administrator. VMConnect's process is elevated, so FancyZones doesn't drag it otherwise 2. Connect to a Hyper-V VM (Windows 11 guest) with Virtual Machine Connection (vmconnect.exe) in an enhanced session. In this mode, resizing the window by dragging its border changes the guest resolution to fit the window. 3. Shift+drag the VMConnect window into a FancyZones zone whose size differs from the current window size. ### ✔️ Expected Behavior The guest resolution changes to fill the window, the same as after resizing the window by its border or snapping it with Windows Snap (dragging it to a screen edge). ### ❌ Actual Behavior The window is resized to the zone, but the guest keeps its previous resolution. If the zone is larger than the window was, the rest of the window stays empty (white). If it is smaller, the guest display is cut off. ### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file _No response_ ### Additional Information - OS: Windows 11 Pro for Workstations, build 26200 - Running as admin: Yes This was reported before in #4336, which was closed as Resolution-External, and in #10827, which was closed as a duplicate. Hyper-V Connection is still listed under [Applications that can't be zoned](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/powertoys/fancyzones#applications-that-cant-be-zoned) in the FancyZones docs. The last comment on #9040 describes the same symptom. The cause is the order of window messages, and FancyZones can fix it on its side. **What happens** - In an enhanced session, VMConnect applies a new window size to the guest only when a move/size loop ends (`WM_EXITSIZEMOVE`), and only if the client size changed since the loop started (`WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE`). A resize outside a move/size loop only re-lays out VMConnect's own menu and status bar. The guest display keeps its size, which leaves the empty area. - Windows Snap by mouse works because Windows applies the snap rectangle before the drag's move/size loop ends. VMConnect sees `WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE`, then the size change, then `WM_EXITSIZEMOVE`. - FancyZones snaps only after the loop has ended. It learns about the drop from `EVENT_SYSTEM_MOVESIZEEND` and then calls `SetWindowPlacement`. By then VMConnect has already handled `WM_EXITSIZEMOVE` with an unchanged size. - Windows' own snapping from the Snap Layouts flyout (hovering the maximize button) has the same problem, because it doesn't involve a move/size loop either. **How I confirmed it** I resized the VMConnect window from a script: - `SetWindowPos` alone: the window is resized, the guest resolution doesn't change. This is the same result as with FancyZones. - The same `SetWindowPos` with `WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE` sent before and `WM_EXITSIZEMOVE` sent after it: the guest resolution follows the window. **Proposed fix** When a snap ends a mouse drag, FancyZones sends `WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE` before and `WM_EXITSIZEMOVE` after applying the zone, so the app sees the same sequence as with Windows Snap. I tested this with a Hyper-V VM and will open a PR. **Note on elevation** On my machine VMConnect's process token is elevated (at medium integrity level). FancyZones checks token elevation, so it only drags VMConnect when PowerToys runs as administrator. Otherwise it shows the "can't drag elevated window" notification. ### Other Software Hyper-V Virtual Machine Connection (vmconnect.exe) 10.0.26100.9278, enhanced session, Windows 11 guest

Connect to a Hyper-V VM (Windows 11 guest) with Virtual Machine Connection (vmconnect.exe) in an enhanced session. In this mode, resizing the window by dragging its border changes the guest resolution to fit the window. 3. Shift+drag the VMConnect window into a FancyZones zone whose size differs from the current window size. ### ✔️ Expected Behavior The guest resolution changes to fill the window, the same as after resizing the window by its border or snapping it with Windows Snap (dragging it to a screen edge). ### ❌ Actual Behavior The window is resized to the zone, but the guest keeps its previous resolution. If the zone is larger than the window was, the rest of the window stays empty (white). If it is smaller, the guest display is cut off. ### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file _No response_ ### Additional Information - OS: Windows 11 Pro for Workstations, build 26200 - Running as admin: Yes This was reported before in #4336, which was closed as Resolution-External, and in #10827, which was closed as a duplicate. The last comment on #9040 describes the same symptom. The cause is the order of window messages, and FancyZones can fix it on its side. **What happens** - In an enhanced session, VMConnect applies a new window size to the guest only when a move/size loop ends (`WM_EXITSIZEMOVE`), and only if the client size changed since the loop started (`WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE`). A resize outside a move/size loop only re-lays out VMConnect's own menu and status bar. The guest display keeps its size, which leaves the empty area. - Windows Snap by mouse works because Windows applies the snap rectangle before the drag's move/size loop ends. VMConnect sees `WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE`, then the size change, then `WM_EXITSIZEMOVE`. - FancyZones snaps only after the loop has ended. It learns about the drop from `EVENT_SYSTEM_MOVESIZEEND` and then calls `SetWindowPlacement`. By then VMConnect has already handled `WM_EXITSIZEMOVE` with an unchanged size. - Windows' own snapping from the Snap Layouts flyout (hovering the maximize button) has the same problem, because it doesn't involve a move/size loop either. **How I confirmed it** I resized the VMConnect window from a script: - `SetWindowPos` alone: the window is resized, the guest resolution doesn't change. This is the same result as with FancyZones. - The same `SetWindowPos` with `WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE` sent before and `WM_EXITSIZEMOVE` sent after it: the guest resolution follows the window. **Proposed fix** When a snap ends a mouse drag, FancyZones sends `WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE` before and `WM_EXITSIZEMOVE` after applying the zone, so the app sees the same sequence as with Windows Snap. I tested this with a Hyper-V VM and will open a PR. **Note on elevation** On my machine VMConnect's process token is elevated (at medium integrity level). FancyZones checks token elevation, so it only drags VMConnect when PowerToys runs as administrator. body_text:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Rather than have separate instances of the CmdPal-Dock on each monitor, allow the option to duplicate / mirror one dock on one or more other monitors. Add an option when selecting each monitor if it should mirror another monitor and specify which other monitor. Mirroring would then inherit the same position and settings of the source monitor.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Sometimes it helps just to have quick access to a few things, but if I have to move the mouse way over the otherside of my screen to get to a dock on a different monitor, then that is no longer quick. Sure I can duplicate a dock manually, but then any changes have to be duplicated as well.

### Supporting information

Example useage:
+ Monitor 1 (Primary) has the dock defined
+ Monitors 2 & 3 both mirror Monitor 1
+ Monitor 4 has it's own dock
+ Monitor 5 has no dock
+ Monitor 6 mirrors Monitor 4

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I'd like to hold Shift while dragging and shaking a File Explorer window by its title bar to bring all open File Explorer windows into that window as tabs.

Any existing tabs in the other windows should come across too. The window being shaken should stay active, with its current tab still selected.

It would work like the familiar window shake gesture, but holding Shift would merge Explorer windows instead of minimising other windows. A configurable keyboard shortcut for the same action would also be useful.

### Scenario when this would be used?

I often end up with several File Explorer windows open while working across different folders. Once things get cluttered, I'd like to gather them into one window without dragging each tab across individually.

Holding Shift and shaking the window I want to keep would be a quick, easy way to tidy things up while keeping all my folders open.

### Supporting information

The idea builds on the existing title bar shake gesture, so it would feel familiar. Holding Shift makes it a deliberate action and keeps it separate from the normal shake behaviour.

This could be an optional PowerToys feature, with settings to enable the gesture and choose a keyboard shortcut.

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

Microsoft PowerToys version: 0.101.2522 Release channel: Stable

### Installation method

Microsoft Store

### Area(s) with issue?

Advanced Paste

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install PowerToys 0.101.2522 from the Microsoft Store.
2. Open PowerToys Settings > Advanced Paste.
3. Configure the OpenAI provider and select the gpt-4o model.
4. Copy some text to the clipboard.
5. Open Advanced Paste and select an AI Paste action.
6. The AI Paste operation fails with the following error:

   "OpenAI request failed with status code: 403"

I independently tested the same OpenAI API key and Project outside PowerToys.

The results were:

- POST /v1/moderations → HTTP 403 Forbidden
- POST /v1/chat/completions → HTTP 200 OK
- POST /v1/chat/completions with inline moderation
  (moderation.model = "omni-moderation-latest") → HTTP 200 OK

The inline moderation request returned valid moderation results using omni-moderation-latest.


### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Advanced Paste should successfully perform the requested AI action when the OpenAI API key, Project, and model are valid and the required moderation functionality is available.

In particular, Advanced Paste should not fail solely because the direct /v1/moderations endpoint returns HTTP 403 when inline moderation through Chat Completions or Responses succeeds with the same API key and Project.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Advanced Paste fails with the following error:

"OpenAI request failed with status code: 403"

I investigated the OpenAI API independently using the same API key and the same Project.

The results are:

- POST /v1/moderations → HTTP 403 Forbidden
- POST /v1/chat/completions → HTTP 200 OK
- POST /v1/chat/completions with:
  {"moderation":{"model":"omni-moderation-latest"}}
  → HTTP 200 OK

The successful inline moderation request returned valid moderation results for both the input and output, using omni-moderation-latest.

This indicates that omni-moderation-latest itself is available and working, while the direct /v1/moderations endpoint returns 403.

PowerToys Advanced Paste v0.101.2522 uses PromptModerationService, which directly calls /v1/moderations with omni-moderation-latest. As a result, this endpoint-specific 403 prevents AI Paste from working.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

OpenAI Support was contacted about this issue.

They confirmed that omni-moderation-latest itself is available, and recommended sharing this issue with the PowerToys developers because PowerToys currently calls the /v1/moderations endpoint directly.

The important distinction is:

- Direct /v1/moderations → HTTP 403 Forbidden
- Chat Completions → HTTP 200 OK
- Chat Completions + inline moderation using omni-moderation-latest → HTTP 200 OK

The successful inline moderation request returned moderation results for both input and output.

Request ID for the successful inline moderation request:
req_a13942a3cc5d4571a3dc07a26c66ca68

Based on the PowerToys source code, PromptModerationService directly uses omni-moderation-latest through /v1/moderations.

Therefore, I would like to ask whether PowerToys could support inline moderation through Chat Completions or Responses instead of relying exclusively on the direct /v1/moderations endpoint.

No API key or other credentials are included in this report.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

A module that watches typing and automatically switches the Japanese IME between Japanese input (hiragana) and direct English input, so the user never has to press 半角/全角 (Hankaku/Zenkaku) or 英数/かな.

- While the user types in romaji (e.g. "kyouha"), the text is composed as Japanese ("今日は").
- When the typed sequence is clearly an English word or code-like token (e.g. "GitHub", "push", "npm install", "localhost"), it is committed as-is in half-width alphanumerics.
- Mixed sentences such as "今日は GitHub に push した" can be typed without any manual mode switching.
- Optional: insert a half-width space around English words (configurable, off by default).
- Per-app exclusion list and an easy toggle, like other PowerToys modules.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Japanese developers and office workers constantly mix Japanese and English terms (product names, commands, code identifiers). Today they must toggle the IME mode many times per sentence, and frequently end up with output like "ぷsh" or "ｇいてゅｂ" and have to retype it.

This is especially common in chat tools, commit messages, issue trackers and AI assistant prompts.

### Supporting information

- Related but different requests: #14850 and #47427 (manual conversion between keyboard layouts, not IME mode detection), #33774 (key mappings per IME).
- Third-party open-source tools that do this already exist, but because such a tool must read all keystrokes system-wide, many users (and corporate IT policies) are only comfortable using it if it is a signed, first-party Microsoft component. This is the main reason for asking for it in PowerToys or in Microsoft IME itself.

body_text: ### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel v0.101.2362 ### Installation method GitHub ### Area(s) with issue? Mouse Without Borders ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open PowerToys Settings and go to Mouse Without Borders. 2. Set a shortcut for Shortcut to toggle Easy Mouse. 3. Verify that the shortcut works correctly. 4. Click the pencil icon to edit the shortcut. 5. Click the ✕ Clear button. 6. The shortcut is successfully cleared and becomes unassigned. 7. Try to assign a new shortcut by pressing a valid key combination, such as Ctrl+Alt+M, Shift+M, or another supported combination. 8. The shortcut editor does not detect or accept any key input, and the shortcut cannot be assigned again. ### ✔️ Expected Behavior After using ✕ Clear, the shortcut should become unassigned, but the shortcut editor should continue to accept keyboard input so that a new shortcut can be assigned. ### ❌ Actual Behavior The ✕ Clear operation itself works correctly and removes the existing shortcut. However, after clearing the shortcut, the shortcut editor stops accepting all keyboard input. No key combination is detected, including combinations using Win, Shift, Ctrl, or Alt. The shortcut cannot be assigned again through the settings UI. This issue occurs only when an existing shortcut is cleared using ✕ Clear. The following operations continue to work normally: - Assigning a shortcut to a field that was originally unassigned. - Changing an existing shortcut directly to another shortcut without using ✕ Clear first. ### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file [PowerToysReport_2026-10-07-15-17-07.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33141399/PowerToysReport_2026-10-07-15-17-07.zip) ### Additional Information - Windows display language: Japanese - Keyboard layout: US keyboard - The shortcut worked normally before it was cleared. - The issue appears specifically after using the ✕ Clear button. ### Other Software _No response_
