body_text: Five example rules, entered through the current release's text box. The new editor would refuse the last four. ### Description of the new feature / enhancement The "IP address mapping" setting of Mouse Without Borders is a plain text box with one "machine-name address" rule per line. Nothing tells whether a line was understood, or whether Mouse Without Borders used it. Several mistakes fail silently: - a rule written for this PC instead of the other machine; - a misspelt machine name; - an address that is read differently from how it is written: `192.168.1` is read as `192.168.0.1`, and `010.0.0.1` as `8.0.0.1` (a leading zero means octal); - an address outside this PC's network while "Same subnet only" is on, which makes Mouse Without Borders skip the machine entirely, without even trying its name; - until #51127, a list that held a single rule was ignored altogether. Proposal: show each rule as a card with a status line, and add or edit rules in a small dialog that checks the input as it is typed. - A card can say: **Connected through this address**, or **Connected through 10.5.0.3 instead**; **Connecting...**; **Not connected: this address didn't answer** or **Not connected: the security keys don't match**; **Not used**, with the reason (no address, an unreadable address, a rule for this PC); **This PC won't try to connect to this machine** (the "Same subnet only" case above); **No machine named X in your device layout yet**; **Mouse Without Borders reads this as 192.168.0.1**. Every status is text plus an icon, never colour alone. - The editor has a machine name field that suggests the machines of the device layout, an IP address field, and a message under each field. It won't save a rule that Mouse Without Borders can't use: Save stays disabled while the address is missing, isn't an IP address or would be read as a different one, or while the name is this PC or contains a space. Mistakes are caught while typing, instead of failing silently later. A name that isn't in the device layout yet (which may be a typo) and an address outside the network with "Same subnet only" on get a warning but can be saved, since both can be intended. Delete is in each card's "..." menu, with the usual confirmation. - The rules are stored as today: one "name address" line each, in the same setting. A line that is not edited is written back unchanged, including lines Mouse Without Borders cannot use, so nothing typed earlier is lost. - The status needs no new channel. Settings already asks Mouse Without Borders for the state of each machine twice a second, for the device tiles. The answer gains an optional address (left out when there is none, so the message stays compatible both ways), and it reports the connection attempt that got furthest instead of the first one that is not idle. ### Scenario when this would be used? Two or more PCs where finding a machine by its name is unreliable: different networks or subnets, a VPN, or no local name resolution. The user maps machine names to addresses by hand. Today a typo or a wrong address shows no error; the machines just do not connect, and the only clue is in the log. With a status per rule the user sees at once whether a rule is used, and which address the machine is reached through. ### Supporting information - Related: #43841 (not connecting across different networks or subnets), #43274 and #35490 (machines that cannot find each other), #51127 (the mapping was ignored when it held a single rule), and the overview #51077. - A working implementation is ready in my fork: two commits (the rule parsing shared between Mouse Without Borders and Settings, plus the address in the status report; then the cards, the dialog and the strings), with 118 new unit tests. I would open a pull request if this direction is welcome. It builds on #51127. - Would you take it as one pull request, or would you prefer the Mouse Without Borders side (the shared parsing and the status report) first, on its own? Written with AI assistance.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

## Summary

I would like to propose a built-in **Snippets extension** for PowerToys Command Palette.

The goal is to allow users to intentionally save frequently used text, find it using partial information, and quickly paste it into the previously focused application.

This proposal is related to the Snippets entry in #38530.

I have prepared a V1 design and would be happy to contribute to the implementation, subject to feedback from the maintainers.

## Design Principle

**Collection is for organization. Search is for retrieval.**

Users should not need to remember the exact snippet name or which collection contains it.

## Proposed V1 Features

### Snippet Management
- Create, edit, and delete plain text snippets.
- Automatically generate a name from the content, while allowing manual editing.
- Create snippets from clipboard text.
- Allow duplicate snippet names and content.
- Confirm before permanently deleting a snippet.

### Collections
- Organize snippets into optional, single-level collections.
- Create, rename, and delete collections.
- Each snippet belongs to at most one collection.
- Deleting a collection moves its snippets to Uncategorized without deleting the snippets.
- Search across all collections by default.

### Search
- Search across snippet names, content, and collection names.
- Support partial matches and fuzzy matching.
- Prioritize strong name matches over content and collection matches.
- Use substring matching primarily for snippet content, with fuzzy matching as a supplementary mechanism.
- Support multiple search terms.

### Clipboard Integration
- **Enter:** Paste the selected snippet into the previously focused application.
- **Copy:** Copy the snippet to the clipboard without automatically pasting it.

### Storage
- JSON-based persistence with schema versioning.
- Separation of UI, snippet management, and persistence.
- An extensible data model for future content types.

## Scope

V1 would support **plain text snippets only**.

Potential future enhancements include image snippets, rich text, tags, aliases, import/export, and variable expansion.

The initial implementation would use Command Palette's existing pages and forms rather than introducing a separate management window.

### Scenario when this would be used?

I frequently reuse text such as email templates, support responses, code snippets, commands, and other predefined messages.

Traditional snippet managers often organize saved content into folders or collections. However, after accumulating many snippets, I may remember part of the content but forget its exact name or which folder contains it.

For example, I might remember that I saved a response containing "currently investigating", but not remember its name or collection.

With the proposed Snippets extension, I could:

1. Open Command Palette.
2. Open Snippets.
3. Type "investigating" or another remembered fragment.
4. Find the matching snippet, regardless of its collection.
5. Press Enter to paste it directly into the previously focused application.

This would eliminate the need to navigate through folders or remember predefined keywords.

**Clipboard History does not fully address this use case**, because it primarily focuses on previously copied content, whereas Snippets provides an intentionally curated collection of reusable content.

I believe this would be useful for developers, support staff, office workers, and anyone who frequently reuses text.

### Supporting information

## Related Issues

- #38530 — Command Palette extension requests, including built-in Snippets.
- #26970 — Previous text snippets feature request.

I previously expressed interest in implementing Snippets in #38530 on September 22, 2026.

## Design Refinements

Since my original comment in #38530, I've refined the V1 design to keep the initial implementation simple.

- **Search:** Instead of requiring users to define keywords, snippets would be searchable by name, content, and collection name, with fuzzy matching where appropriate.
- **Collections:** V1 would use single-level collections rather than hierarchical folders.
- **Content types:** V1 would focus on plain text, with image support considered for future versions.

The original goal remains unchanged: users should be able to find and reuse snippets without remembering where they were saved.

## Proposed Implementation Approach

I would like to follow existing PowerToys built-in extension patterns wherever possible.

- **Bookmarks:** Use as a reference for registration/editing forms, management, and JSON persistence.
- **Clipboard History / Advanced Paste:** Investigate reuse of existing clipboard and paste mechanisms.
- **Command Palette Toolkit:** Use existing commands, pages, and `StringMatcher` functionality for search.
- **Dynamic List Page:** Handle searching snippet names, content, and collections with custom ranking.

The exact implementation details would be confirmed against the latest PowerToys source before development.

The design intentionally keeps V1 relatively small while allowing future extensions.

## Feedback Requested

Before beginning implementation, I would appreciate guidance from the maintainers:

1. Is anyone already working on a built-in Snippets extension?
2. Does this proposed functionality and general design align with the direction of Command Palette?
3. Would the maintainers be open to reviewing a contribution based on this proposal?
4. Are there any existing components or architectural conventions that I should follow?

I am happy to adjust the design based on feedback.

**I would be glad to contribute the implementation if this approach is considered appropriate.**

Thank you for your time and consideration!

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Original power toys had an auto log on setting. Many people find it annoying when using several computers to have to "log on" when booting up.
Personally I have 7 computers running for several reasons and only one needs me to enter a code on startup - don't need to do that and can't find a way to by-pass that requirement.

### Scenario when this would be used?

I use 5 computers and sometimes more and it is irritating and annoying to have to sign in or log-on only one computer (newest and latest copy of Windows 11 pro.

### Supporting information

This "sign-on or log-on" has really screwed up my network as it is the only computer that requires me to enter a code on start up and I can't use it to transfer files across the network.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Please implement a direct, customizable keyboard shortcut (e.g., `Ctrl + Shift + R`) to instantly open PowerRename for whatever files are currently highlighted or selected in Windows File Explorer. 
Currently, keyboard users are forced to simulate a right-click via `Shift + F10`, use the arrow keys or press a letter key, and then either hit `Enter` or click the Left Mouse Button (LMB) just to pass the selection into PowerRename. The letter navigation often breaks, and requiring a mouse click completely defeats the purpose of an efficient, keyboard-centric power-user workflow.

### Scenario when this would be used?

This is crucial for power users who bulk-rename files multiple times a day. Forcing a mouse interaction or navigating multi-tier context menus slows down productivity significantly.

### Supporting information

Other PowerToys utilities like Peek or Color Picker feature a native global shortcut trigger. Adding a direct trigger to launch PowerRename targeting active File Explorer selections would make the utility significantly faster and truly mouse-free.

body_text:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I would like to be able to configure custom minimum and maximum brightness values in PowerMonitor, rather than always using the full 0–100% range.

For example, I would like to set the brightness range to 1–100%, so the slider never sets the monitor brightness to 0%.

Some monitors interpret 0% brightness as turning the display off entirely, rather than simply setting it to the lowest usable brightness. A configurable minimum brightness would prevent accidental display shutdowns when adjusting brightness.

Ideally, users could configure both the minimum and maximum brightness limits, with the slider operating within the selected range. The default behavior could remain unchanged for users who do not configure custom limits.



### Scenario when this would be used?

When adjusting monitor brightness through PowerMonitor, accidentally reaching 0% can turn off the display completely on certain monitors.

This is particularly inconvenient when using the brightness slider or making small adjustments, as the display may go dark instead of remaining at its minimum usable brightness.

Setting a custom minimum of 1% would prevent this issue while preserving normal brightness adjustment functionality.

### Supporting information

Example configuration:

Minimum brightness: 1%

Maximum brightness: 100%

The feature could be implemented as configurable minimum and maximum limits for the brightness slider, with the selected range mapped to the corresponding brightness values supported by the monitor.

This would be especially useful for monitors where 0% brightness effectively turns the display off.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Would an opt-in [Parallel Search MCP](https://docs.parallel.ai/integrations/mcp/search-mcp) provider fit Command Palette's Web Search extension? It would show source titles, URLs and short excerpts in the palette, with an action to open each result in the browser. Parallel provides free web search without an account or API key; anonymous searches use Fast mode.

The proposed integration would be disabled by default and preserve existing browser search, custom search URLs and history. Queries would be sent to Parallel only after an explicit search action in the opt-in mode, rather than on every keystroke. This would require an HTTP MCP client path; the current extension opens browser search URLs.

### Scenario when this would be used?

A user looking for a documentation page could inspect a few source excerpts and choose the relevant page without first opening a browser results page. This relates to #41581, but proposes source results rather than generated answers, weather widgets or currency conversion.

### Supporting information

The existing implementation is [WebSearchListPage.cs](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/ccdd9b19ca980e9d383a42c235fa313a595ac712/src/modules/cmdpal/ext/Microsoft.CmdPal.Ext.WebSearch/Pages/WebSearchListPage.cs). I'd keep the first version limited to search results and test the opt-in path, cancellation, timeouts, rate-limit errors and preservation of existing settings. Page fetching and answer generation would be outside this proposal.

I'd like feedback on whether this belongs in the built-in extension or should be a separate community extension before implementation or a spec. I work at Parallel.

body_text:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Windows lacks a native mechanism to automatically switch monitor refresh rates on a per-application basis or revert to a designated default when switching focus back to the desktop.

This utility would allow users to:

Set a Default Desktop Refresh Rate: Define a global fallback refresh rate (e.g., 60Hz or 120Hz for power savings, lower heat, or improved multi-monitor stability) for normal desktop usage.

Per-App Refresh Rate Overrides: Map specific executable files (.exe) to target refresh rates (e.g., locking a competitive game to 240Hz or 360Hz).

Automatic Focus Detection: Listen for foreground window focus changes using Windows hook APIs. When a mapped executable gains focus, the display dynamically switches to its assigned refresh rate, and reverts back to the default rate when minimized or closed.

Multi-Monitor Support: Optionally choose which connected display target to modify.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Gaming & High-Refresh Rate Displays: A user running a 240Hz monitor may want their desktop locked to 60Hz/120Hz to reduce GPU power draw and fan noise. When launching a fast-paced game (e.g., VALORANT or CS2), PowerToys automatically elevates the display rate to 240Hz. Upon switching back to Discord or web browsing, the screen safely returns to the baseline rate.   Video Playback & Productivity: Locking specific media players (e.g., VLC, MPC-HC) or video editor applications to 24Hz, 48Hz, or 60Hz to prevent stutter caused by frame-rate misalignment, without needing to manually modify Windows Display Settings every time.

### Supporting information

Implementation Feasibility: Windows exposes Win32 display configuration APIs (EnumDisplaySettings and ChangeDisplaySettingsEx) as well as modern WinRT Display Monitor APIs capable of programmatic, low-latency refresh rate adjustments.

Existing Alternatives: Current solutions rely on outdated standalone third-party tools, GPU driver-level profiles (which often fail to trigger properly with modern borderless-window modes), or custom command-line scripts. Integrating this into PowerToys provides a clean, secure, and maintained system-level utility.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

The current incremental loading trigger does not account for cases where the loaded items are insufficient to make the container scrollable.

This affects both ListView and GridView, although it is more likely to occur with GridView, which can display multiple items per row.

If the initial batch of items does not fill the available viewport, incremental loading is never triggered because the container cannot scroll, even though more items are available.

### Repro steps

1. Create a page with a small grid layout and enable "load more" behavior, adding 20 items per load.
1. Open the page and observe that only the first batch is loaded.
1. Be sad.

### Expected behavior

Incremental loading should continue requesting items until:

The viewport is filled and scrolling becomes possible.
All available items have been loaded.

This should work consistently for both ListView and GridView.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

A Power Toys add-on that allows someone to launch a virtual desktop as a different user. This would allow someone to run a virtual desktop and all of the applications in that desktop as a different user.

### Scenario when this would be used?

The scenario would be a DBA or sys admin running the base desktop as their "regular user" while running a virtual desktop as their admin user. The virtual desktop would allow them to access systems/databases with a different set of credentials, thus maintaining good security posture, but not have to launch every tool individually as a different user.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

PowerToys has useful system-monitoring features, but it does not show the computer's current power usage. I would like to request a lightweight Power Consumption Monitor module or Command Palette extension. It should display the current estimated power draw in real time, including CPU package power, GPU power, and battery discharge rate when available. If the OS or hardware exposes total system power, it should show that value directly. Otherwise, it should show an estimate based on available sensors and clearly label it as "Estimated." Users should be able to pin the reading to the Command Palette Dock, view it in a flyout, or choose which metrics to display. The monitor should update every 1–2 seconds and use minimal system resources.

### Scenario when this would be used?

While gaming, rendering, or running heavy workloads, to see whether the system is drawing a lot of power or getting close to the PSU limit.
When undervolting, overclocking, or tuning fan curves, to compare power usage before and after changes.
When troubleshooting high fan noise or overheating, to check whether high power draw is the cause.
When using a laptop on battery, to monitor power consumption and estimate remaining battery life.
When trying to reduce electricity usage or choose a more efficient power plan.
When comparing different hardware configurations or settings.

### Supporting information

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

A new PowerToy that lets you change the icon File Explorer shows for a file type, without touching the registry by hand.

- Pick a target by extension (`.psd`, `.md`, `.code-workspace`, ...) or by ProgId, and assign an icon from an `.ico` / `.dll` / `.exe` (with index) / image file.
- Same for folders: override the generic folder icon, or set a per-folder icon.
- Preview the icon at 16/32/48/256 px before applying.
- Applying writes `HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\<.ext>\DefaultIcon` (and `ProgId\DefaultIcon` when the extension maps to one), then refreshes the shell icon cache via `SHChangeNotify(SHCNE_ASSOCCHANGED)` so the change shows up without killing `explorer.exe`.
- One-click "Restore default" per entry, plus a list of every override currently applied, so changes are auditable and reversible.
- Export / import the whole set as a small JSON theme, so a setup can be moved between machines.

### Scenario when this would be used?

I work in File Explorer all day and my folders are full of code-ish file types: `.code-workspace`, `.ps1`, `.md`, `.json`, `.gitignore`, `.env`, `.sln`, plus game/engine assets. Most of them render as the same blank white page, so I have to read file names instead of recognizing icons — that's slow when scanning a folder of mixed types.

Today the only way is manual registry work, and it's painful and risky:

1. `regedit` → `HKCR` → find the extension → find its ProgId → edit `DefaultIcon`.
2. Force Explorer to drop its icon cache (`ie4uinit.exe -show`, restarting `explorer.exe`, ...).
3. Repeat for every extension — with no record of what was changed, and no clean way back to the defaults.

A typo there can break icons or file associations, and nothing warns you. PowerToys already ships per-user settings, backup/restore, and Explorer-facing modules, so a guided and reversible UI for this fits naturally and complements the existing File Explorer add-ons.

### Supporting information

- Related open requests: #34493 ("Change File Icon") and #41964 ("folder icon/color change"). This request adds the reversible/auditable side (list of overrides + restore default + export/import) and the icon-cache refresh step, which the existing requests do not cover.
- Registry keys involved: `HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\<.ext>\DefaultIcon`, `HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\<ProgId>\DefaultIcon` — value format `path,index`.
- Per-folder icons use `desktop.ini` → `[.ShellClassInfo] IconResource=...`.
- Icon sources Windows already accepts: `.ico`, `.dll`/`.exe` + index, images convertible to `.ico`.
- Documented cache refresh: `SHChangeNotify(SHCNE_ASSOCCHANGED, SHCNF_IDLIST, nullptr, nullptr)`.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Title:
[Mouse Utilities] Option to auto-hide mouse cursor after X seconds of inactivity

Description / Proposed Feature:
Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
When reading documents, watching content, or focusing on work without typing, the mouse cursor often remains visible on the screen. Currently, Windows only offers the option to hide the pointer while typing, but there is no built-in option or PowerToys feature to hide the cursor automatically after a set period of inactivity.

Describe the solution you'd like
I would like to propose a new feature under Mouse Utilities that automatically hides the mouse cursor after a user-defined period of inactivity (e.g., 5, 10, or 30 seconds).
Key features could include:

An enable/disable toggle in Mouse Utilities.

A configurable timer (e.g., slider or numerical input for seconds of idle time).

Automatic reappearance of the cursor as soon as mouse movement or clicking is detected.

Describe alternatives you've considered
Third-party tools exist for this specific purpose (such as AutoHideMouseCursor), but having this functionality natively integrated into PowerToys would provide a cleaner, more reliable, and lightweight experience for Windows users without needing additional standalone software.

### Scenario when this would be used?

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

v0.101.2362

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

FancyZones

### Steps to reproduce

Dragging a window onto a Fancy Zone while holding the shift key makes the visual zones disapear. After that I can no longer get any zones to show up. I can restart it by disableing Zancy Zones in Powertoys settings, and then enable it again. and it all "crashes" when I make a new window drag onto a Zone.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Normally I can drag and drop windows onto the zones without any problems

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Dragging a window onto a Fancy Zone while holding the shift key makes the visual zones disapear. After that I can no longer get any zones to show up. I can restart it by disableing Zancy Zones in Powertoys settings, and then enable it again. and it all "crashes" when I make a new window drag onto a Zone.

body_text: ### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel 0.98.1 ### Installation method Microsoft Store ### Area(s) with issue? Keyboard Manager ### Steps to reproduce Having a PC with a Japanese physical keyboard, then remap the IME Convert and Non-Convert keys (the ones that sandwiches the space bar) to produce a space instead. If I use my keyboard in Japanese, it works fine, and the keys produce a space. But If I change the layout of my keyboard to AZERTY French, then those keys produce nothing. ### ✔️ Expected Behavior Since those keys exist on my physical layout, I'm expecting the shortcut to work even if the Windows layout is different. ### ❌ Actual Behavior The keys work only on the Japanese layout. ### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file [PowerToysReport_2026-10-14-15-42-27.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33420962/PowerToysReport_2026-10-14-15-42-27.zip) ### Additional Information Windows 11 Home 25H2 Language in English UK with physical Japanese keyboard. Two keyboards layout are registered: French AZERTY and Japanese QWERTY ### Other Software _No response_

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

This deserves to be part of Windows UI. But needs some tuning (to Apple standards) as a UI element....

1) Shake Mouse works well but would benefit from some additional optional "user feedback tested" preset timings and themes.  (I am sure there are some optimal settings - it took me a while to get something that felt natural and looked tidy - there are too many bad options! )

2) The mouse click (down) that dismisses the spotlight should be allow itself to propagated to the underlying app or desktop. Including for double clicks. This would make this a truly visual clue rather than another layer to click through. This could be optional - but is natural to expect if transparency is high.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Overal windows productivity. I hace 3 x 4k monitors at high res. so this is essential app for me.  Its possible to loose the mouse. I naturally shake the mouse device to make it show up - so this feature helps with that natural ui interaction.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I'd like to propose a new replacement pattern in PowerRename. In addition to the existing `$YYYY` etc. for file creation/modification date, a new pattern like `$timestamp` (or `$TS` if a shorter syntax is preferred) will be replaced by a timestamp (seconds since epoch). For example, given a file created at "Wed, 14 Oct 2026 01:23:45.000 GMT", when the "Replace with" pattern is `$timestamp$fff`, then the renamed name should be "1791941025000".

### Scenario when this would be used?

This is useful when an existing system expects files containing UNIX (without milliseconds) or JavaScript (with milliseconds) timestamp in the file name. Also, the timestamp would be timezone-agnostic, unlike the existing date and time fields. It would be a nice addition to the existing file creation/modification date syntax.

body_text: ### Description of the new feature / enhancement In PowerToys utilities - add feature to turn off to new Windows 11 context menu / turn on to old Windows 10 context menu without admin privileges with automatic explorer restart to activate feature ### Scenario when this would be used? When on work you constantly work with options that are hidden in (show more options) it is annoying to click and drag mouse for that one option ### Supporting information Here is the step-by-step guide to doing this safely. Method 1: Manual Registry Edit (Recommended) Open Registry Editor: Press Windows Key + R on your keyboard. Type regedit and press Enter. Click "Yes" if the User Account Control prompt appears. Navigate to this path: Copy and paste the following into the address bar at the top of the Registry Editor window and press Enter: HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Classes\CLSID Create the new Key: Right-click on the CLSID folder in the left sidebar. Select New > Key. Name the new key exactly this: {86ca1aa0-34aa-4e8b-a509-50c905bae2a2} (Note: You must include the curly brackets). Create the InprocServer32 subkey: Right-click on the new key you just created ({86ca1aa0...}). Select New > Key. Name this subkey: InprocServer32 Modify the Default value: Click on the InprocServer32 folder you just created. On the right side, double-click the entry named (Default). Make sure the "Value data" box is completely empty. Do not type anything in it. Click OK. Restart Windows Explorer: To see the changes immediately, you need to restart Explorer. Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager. Find Windows Explorer in the list. Right-click it and select Restart.

Quick Accent

body_text:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Add a page (in File Explorer add-ons, or as a small utility of its own) that lets users choose which installed preview handler File Explorer uses for each file type.

Proposed behaviour:

1. List file extensions and their effective preview handler: the handler Explorer will actually load after HKCU and HKLM and the extension and ProgID keys are combined, with the source key shown.
2. For any extension, offer a dropdown of every handler registered under `Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\PreviewHandlers` (HKCU and HKLM), including third-party ones, not only PowerToys' own.
3. By default, write the choice as a per-user override under `HKCU\Software\Classes\<ext>\shellex\{8895b1c6-b41f-4c1c-a562-0d564250836f}`, so no elevation is needed and "Reset" simply deletes the override. Offer an "Apply for all users" option (elevated) that writes the HKLM registration instead, since some hosts, such as Outlook and Office, only read preview handlers from HKLM (see #17273).
4. Optionally, a "Keep my choice" toggle that notices when an installer or app update changes the handler for a pinned type and restores the user's choice (or notifies them).

The same pattern would extend naturally to thumbnail providers (`{e357fccd-a995-4576-b01f-234630154e96}`), but this request is only for preview handlers.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Windows has no UI for this. Whichever app registered last owns the preview pane for a file type, so installing or updating one app silently replaces another's previewer. For example, with both PDF-XChange Editor and SumatraPDF installed, the PDF preview switches between them depending on which one was most recently installed or updated. Users who notice have to find and edit `shellex` registry keys by hand.

PowerToys is part of this problem as well as being the obvious place to fix it. Its own Settings page warns that enabling its preview handlers "will override other preview handlers already installed" (#17273). #17546 is a concrete case: enabling developer file previews replaces a rendering HTML previewer with a source view, and the only fix is to turn the whole feature off.

Windows already protects default *apps* from installer hijacking (the protected UserChoice). Preview handlers, thumbnail providers, and other shell extensions never got the same treatment, so this gap affects PDFs, images, video, Office files, CAD formats, and anything else where more than one app ships a previewer.

### Supporting information

- The only GUI that has ever done this, Stephen Toub's Preview Handler Association Editor (2007), is no longer downloadable from its official link (the attachment now returns 403): https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/archive/blogs/toub/preview-handler-association-editor. A comment on #3799 also reports that it doesn't list PowerToys' handlers, likely because those register per-user in HKCU.
- Registration model this would read and write: https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/shell/how-to-register-a-preview-handler
- Prior discussion: #17546 (a commenter suggested an "extension-to-handler GUI ... as its own PowerToy" that could set both HKCU and HKLM, subject to admin), #3799 (the "tool to manage them" half was closed with the Monaco work), #17683, #17273.
- Relation to #26726: this feature manages Windows' preview handler registrations in general, not PowerToys' own previewers, so it stays useful whatever happens to the PowerToys preview pane handlers. It sits close to Registry Preview and the File Explorer add-ons page, both of which already exist.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

PowerToys already bundles many advanced productivity tools for Windows power users. I would like to propose adding a lightweight memory management utility that exposes the same functionality as RAMMap's "Empty Standby List".

The feature would allow users to quickly flush the Windows Standby Memory Cache without needing to install and run Sysinternals RAMMap.

Suggested capabilities:

Empty Standby List
Optional Empty Modified Page List
Optional Empty Working Sets
Display current memory breakdown:
In Use
Available
Cached
Standby
PowerToys Run command support
Keyboard shortcut support
Optional automatic triggers when available memory falls below a user-defined threshold

This would provide a convenient and modern interface for a function that many power users already rely on through RAMMap.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Many users experience situations where Windows accumulates a large amount of Standby Memory after intensive workloads:

Large Excel workbooks
Power BI models
Visual Studio builds
Data processing workloads
Gaming sessions
Virtual machines
AI and local LLM workloads

While Standby Memory is technically available for reuse, many users encounter situations where applications become sluggish or memory pressure occurs until the Standby List is manually cleared.

Currently the common workflow is:

Download RAMMap.
Launch RAMMap as Administrator.
Navigate to the Empty menu.
Select "Empty Standby List".

This is inconvenient for a task many advanced users perform regularly.

Having the functionality directly available in PowerToys would make it more discoverable, modern, and easier to automate.

### Supporting information

RAMMap already exposes this functionality and has been widely used by Windows power users for years.

Potential implementation options include:

A standalone PowerToys module
A Quick Action in PowerToys Run
A tray menu item
A command line interface integrated with PowerToys Command Palette

Benefits:

Reduced dependency on an additional Sysinternals utility
Better discoverability for power users
Easier automation and shortcuts
Consistent user experience within the Windows power-user ecosystem

Related Sysinternals utility:

RAMMap
Empty Standby List functionality

Many users already rely on this operation as a troubleshooting step before rebooting the computer, particularly when working with memory-intensive applications such as Excel, Power BI, Visual Studio, local AI tools, and virtual machines.

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

`main` @ `57aff29738` (dev build). Found on 2026-10-06 during the System.CommandLine 2.0 GA work (#50884); the same code is on `main` after that PR merged.

### Installation method

Dev build in Visual Studio

### Area(s) with issue?

FancyZones

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build `src\modules\fancyzones\FancyZonesCLI` (x64 Release).
2. Run `FancyZonesCLI.exe set-layout focus --monitor abc`.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

A parse error saying `abc` isn't a valid monitor index, and a non-zero exit code, the same as any other invalid option value.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The command throws an unhandled `System.InvalidOperationException` instead of printing a parse error.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

N/A

### Additional Information

Cause: the `--monitor` validator in `src\modules\fancyzones\FancyZonesCLI\CommandLine\Commands\SetLayoutCommand.cs` only skips when there are no tokens. It then calls `result.GetValueOrDefault<int?>()`, which throws when the token failed to parse as an `int`.

Suggested fix: return early from the validator when the option result already has parse errors, so System.CommandLine reports the normal error.

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

`main` @ `57aff29738` (dev build). Found on 2026-10-06 while validating #51056.

### Installation method

Dev build in Visual Studio

### Area(s) with issue?

General

### Steps to reproduce

1. On a clean clone, run `tools\build\build.ps1 -Platform x64 -Configuration Release -Path src\modules\powerrename\PowerRenameContextMenu`, or build one of the other context-menu projects the same way.
2. Look inside the project folder, then at the MSIX that the build packs.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Intermediates go to the repo-level `x64\Release\TemporaryBuild\obj\<project>\` folder, the same place a solution build or `build-essentials.ps1` puts them. The project folder stays clean, and the MSIX contains only its payload.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

About 1,400 intermediate files land in an `x64\` folder inside the project folder. The next MakeAppx run packs them: the PowerRename MSIX grew from 26 to 1,415 files (17.5 MB). The build still succeeds, so this is easy to miss.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

N/A

### Additional Information

Cause: `build.ps1` builds a single `.vcxproj` without `/p:SolutionDir`, but `build-essentials.ps1` passes it. So `$(SolutionDir)` falls back to the project folder. These projects set `IntDir` under `$(SolutionDir)`:

- `FileLocksmithContextMenu`
- `ImageResizerContextMenu`
- `NewShellExtensionContextMenu`
- `PowerRenameContextMenu`
- `PowerToysSetupCustomActionsVNext`

Several others, mostly native unit-test projects, also put `OutDir` under `$(SolutionDir)`.

Suggested fix: have `build.ps1` pass `/p:SolutionDir=<repo root>\` like `build-essentials.ps1` does, or switch those projects to `$(RepoRoot)`.

N/A

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

`main` @ `57aff29738` (dev build). Found on 2026-10-06 during the System.CommandLine 2.0 GA work (#50884); the same code is on `main` after that PR merged.

### Installation method

Dev build in Visual Studio

### Area(s) with issue?

Image Resizer

### Steps to reproduce

1. Make sure `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\PowerToys\Image Resizer\settings.json` doesn't exist (fresh profile, or rename it).
2. Run `PowerToys.ImageResizerCLI.exe --width 100 --filename "%1_custom" <image>`.
3. Look at the output file name.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The output uses the `--filename` format (`<name>_custom.<ext>`).

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The output uses the default format (`%1 (%2)`), so `-n`/`--filename` is ignored. Running the same command again, once `settings.json` exists, works.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

N/A

### Additional Information

Cause, in `src\modules\imageresizer\ui\Properties\Settings.cs`:

- When `settings.json` doesn't exist, `Settings.Reload()` saves the defaults.
- Serializing reads the public getter-only `FileNameFormat` property, which computes and caches `_fileNameFormat` from the default `FileName`.
- The `FileName` setter never clears that cache, so the value the CLI sets afterwards is never used.

Suggested fix: clear `_fileNameFormat` in the `FileName` setter, and mark `FileNameFormat` `[JsonIgnore]` so serialization doesn't compute it.

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update, GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

Two machines, **both running the same PowerToys version 0.101.2362.0**:

- `MACHINE-A` — has the physical keyboard and mouse (controller / sender)
- `MACHINE-B` — receives input (Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26200, 1920x1200 @ 120 DPI)
- Connected over Wi-Fi, same /24 subnet, direct on-link route (no VPN in path)
- `UseService: true` on `MACHINE-B`

Move the mouse from `MACHINE-A` to `MACHINE-B` and type a sentence at normal speed.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Characters arrive in the order they were typed.


### ❌ Actual Behavior

**Adjacent input events swap places.** Transposition affects characters *and* spaces equally, i.e. it is order-blind rather than character-specific — so this is not a keyboard-layout problem (the characters themselves are always correct):

| typed | received |
|---|---|
| `buchstaben` | `bcuhstaben` |
| `nicht` | `incht` |
| `schreiben` | `schrieben` |
| `es ist` | `e sist` |
| `ich weiß` | `ic hweiß` |
| `zeug an` | `zeu gan` |

Roughly 4–6 transpositions per sentence, continuously — not only during reconnects.

---

### Root cause

MWB maintains **two concurrent TCP connections** to the same peer (one outbound as client, one inbound as server). Both are owned by the *same* MWB process:

```
State        LocalAddress  LocalPort  RemoteAddress  RemotePort  OwningProcess
Established  10.x.x.B      65516      10.x.x.A       15101       13704
Established  10.x.x.B      15101      10.x.x.A       53676       13704
```

`SocketStuff.MainTCPRoutine` runs **per socket**, and input injection happens inside it — confirmed by this stack trace from the module log:

```
System.Runtime.InteropServices.COMException (0x8007007A)
   at WinRT.ExceptionHelpers.<ThrowExceptionForHR>g__Throw|38_0(Int32 hr)
   at MouseWithoutBorders.Class.InputSimulation.SendInputEx(INPUT input)
   at MouseWithoutBorders.Class.InputSimulation.SendMouse(MOUSEDATA md)
   at MouseWithoutBorders.Core.Receiver.ProcessPackage(DATA package, TcpSk tcp)
   at MouseWithoutBorders.Class.SocketStuff.MainTCPRoutine(TcpSk tcp, String machineName, Boolean isClient)
```

So two independent receive threads call `ProcessPackage` → `SendInputEx` concurrently. Nothing serialises them, so two input events that were sent in order can be injected in the opposite order. The observed swap rate matches that.

### Decisive test — forcing a single socket fixes it

Blocking the inbound channel on the receiving machine collapses MWB to one socket and therefore one receive thread:

```powershell
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "MWB-SingleSocket" -Direction Inbound -Action Block `
  -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 15100,15101 -RemoteAddress <peer-ip> -Profile Any
```

- Established connections drop from 2 → 1 within ~30 s.
- **Input still works in both directions** (TCP is bidirectional; the remaining socket carries the input).
- Typed text then arrives **verbatim correct** — zero transpositions for the whole duration of the test.
- Removing the rule restores the second socket, and the transposition returns immediately.

This is a reliable on/off reproduction of the defect.

> Note: this is only a diagnostic, not a usable workaround. Windows Firewall filters connection *setup* only, so after MWB tears down both sockets on a reconnect, both come back during any window in which the rule is absent.

### Suggested fix

Either serialise injection across all receive threads (a single injection queue or a lock around `SendInputEx`), or route all input packets over one designated socket and keep the second connection for control/clipboard traffic only.

---

### Second, related defect: unhandled `SendInputEx` failure tears down the connection

`SendInputEx` fails with `COMException 0x8007007A` (`ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER`) — **105 occurrences in a single day's log**. The exception is not caught in `ProcessPackage`/`SendMouse`, so it propagates into `MainTCPRoutine` and kills the receive loop. The log shows the same sequence every time, within 1–2 seconds:

```
16:17:21  !Exception!: COMException (0x8007007A)   (x2)
16:17:23  SocketStuff.cs::AddSocket::767  New connection from client: [MACHINE-A]
16:17:23  SettingsUtils.cs::SaveSettings::224  Exception encountered while saving settings  (x2)
```

Reconnects per hour from one day's log:

| hour | reconnects | `SendInput` failures |
|---|---|---|
| 11:00 | 7 | 11 |
| 12:00 | 29 | 58 |
| 13:00 | 12 | 23 |
| 14:00 | 4 | 2 |
| 15:00 | 5 | 5 |
| 16:00 | 6 | 6 |

(Clipboard sharing and file transfer were disabled between 13:00 and 14:00 — see "Interaction with existing issues" below.)

Note the failing call is on the **mouse** path (`SendMouse`), yet the user-visible damage is to **typing**, because the connection teardown discards whatever keystrokes are in flight.

A `try`/`catch` around the injection call would stop a single failed input event from destroying the session. The underlying `ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER` from `SendInput` itself still needs separate investigation.

### Interaction with existing issues

- **#49147** (clipboard transfer desyncs the main channel): confirmed here. The log contained **exactly six** `MainTCPRoutine.TcpReceive error, invalid package from [MACHINE-A]: 0` lines before the socket closed, matching the `errCount > 5` threshold in `SocketStuff.cs`. Disabling `ShareClipboard` and `TransferFile` cut reconnects from 29/h to 4–6/h — a large improvement, but it does **not** affect the ordering defect above.
- **#44177** (`UseService` spawns duplicate processes): with `UseService: true` this machine runs two SYSTEM instances (arguments `winlogon` and `default`) plus a helper, and the log contains **59** `settings.json` write-contention errors (`The process cannot access the file ... because it is being used by another process`), so MWB can never persist its machine pool.
- **#33346** (`SendInput` vs `InputInjector` / UIPI): also reproduced. Setting `UseService: false` made mouse movement keep working while clicks and keystrokes stopped on elevated windows, because MWB then runs non-elevated and UIPI blocks injection.

### Ruled out

- **Network** — direct on-link route, ping 2–4 ms, jitter σ = 0.7 ms, no loss; Wi-Fi at 90 % signal / 1201 Mbps with **zero** `WLAN-AutoConfig` events during the measurement window. No relevant entries in the System event log.
- **VPN** — a corporate VPN adapter is present but the route to the peer does not traverse it.
- **Version mismatch** — both machines run the identical PowerToys build.
- **Keyboard layout** — the received characters are always correct, only their order is wrong.
- **Resource leak** — handle counts rose during error bursts but were released again (1655 → 989 with no process restart), so this is not a monotonic leak.

With `UseService: true` the SYSTEM instances log outside the user profile:

```
C:\Windows\System32\config\systemprofile\AppData\Local\Microsoft\PowerToys\
    MouseWithoutBorders\Logs\<version>\<guid>Log_<yyyy-MM-dd>.log
```

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

_No response_

### Other Software

The same machine pair, in its previous generation, ran the standalone Microsoft Garage *Mouse without Borders* 2.x and did not show this behaviour. The problem appeared after both ends moved to the PowerToys module.

```
   at MouseWithoutBorders.Core.Receiver.ProcessPackage(DATA package, TcpSk tcp)
   at MouseWithoutBorders.Class.SocketStuff.MainTCPRoutine(TcpSk tcp, String machineName, Boolean isClient)
```

So two independent receive threads call `ProcessPackage` → `SendInputEx` concurrently. Nothing serialises them, so two input events that were sent in order can be injected in the opposite order. The observed swap rate matches that.

### Decisive test — forcing a single socket fixes it

Blocking the inbound channel on the receiving machine collapses MWB to one socket and therefore one receive thread:

```powershell
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "MWB-SingleSocket" -Direction Inbound -Action Block `
  -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 15100,15101 -RemoteAddress <peer-ip> -Profile Any
```

- Established connections drop from 2 → 1 within ~30 s.
- **Input still works in both directions** (TCP is bidirectional; the remaining socket carries the input).
- Typed text then arrives **verbatim correct** — zero transpositions for the whole duration of the test.
- Removing the rule restores the second socket, and the transposition returns immediately.

This is a reliable on/off reproduction of the defect.

> Note: this is only a diagnostic, not a usable workaround. Windows Firewall filters connection *setup* only, so after MWB tears down both sockets on a reconnect, both come back during any window in which the rule is absent.

### Suggested fix

Either serialise injection across all receive threads (a single injection queue or a lock around `SendInputEx`), or route all input packets over one designated socket and keep the second connection for control/clipboard traffic only.

---

### Second, related defect: unhandled `SendInputEx` failure tears down the connection

`SendInputEx` fails with `COMException 0x8007007A` (`ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER`) — **105 occurrences in a single day's log**. The exception is not caught in `ProcessPackage`/`SendMouse`, so it propagates into `MainTCPRoutine` and kills the receive loop. The log shows the same sequence every time, within 1–2 seconds:

```
16:17:21  !Exception!: COMException (0x8007007A)   (x2)
16:17:23  SocketStuff.cs::AddSocket::767  New connection from client: [MACHINE-A]
16:17:23  SettingsUtils.cs::SaveSettings::224  Exception encountered while saving settings  (x2)
```

Reconnects per hour from one day's log:

| hour | reconnects | `SendInput` failures |
|---|---|---|
| 11:00 | 7 | 11 |
| 12:00 | 29 | 58 |
| 13:00 | 12 | 23 |
| 14:00 | 4 | 2 |
| 15:00 | 5 | 5 |
| 16:00 | 6 | 6 |

(Clipboard sharing and file transfer were disabled between 13:00 and 14:00 — see "Interaction with existing issues" below.)

Note the failing call is on the **mouse** path (`SendMouse`), yet the user-visible damage is to **typing**, because the connection teardown discards whatever keystrokes are in flight.

A `try`/`catch` around the injection call would stop a single failed input event from destroying the session. The underlying `ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER` from `SendInput` itself still needs separate investigation.

### Interaction with existing issues

- **#49147** (clipboard transfer desyncs the main channel): confirmed here. The log contained **exactly six** `MainTCPRoutine.TcpReceive error, invalid package from [MACHINE-A]: 0` lines before the socket closed, matching the `errCount > 5` threshold in `SocketStuff.cs`. Disabling `ShareClipboard` and `TransferFile` cut reconnects from 29/h to 4–6/h — a large improvement, but it does **not** affect the ordering defect above.
- **#44177** (`UseService` spawns duplicate processes): with `UseService: true` this machine runs two SYSTEM instances (arguments `winlogon` and `default`) plus a helper, and the log contains **59** `settings.json` write-contention errors (`The process cannot access the file ... because it is being used by another process`), so MWB can never persist its machine pool.
- **#33346** (`SendInput` vs `InputInjector` / UIPI): also reproduced. Setting `UseService: false` made mouse movement keep working while clicks and keystrokes stopped on elevated windows, because MWB then runs non-elevated and UIPI blocks injection.

### Ruled out

- **Network** — direct on-link route, ping 2–4 ms, jitter σ = 0.7 ms, no loss; Wi-Fi at 90 % signal / 1201 Mbps with **zero** `WLAN-AutoConfig` events during the measurement window. No relevant entries in the System event log.
- **VPN** — a corporate VPN adapter is present but the route to the peer does not traverse it.
- **Version mismatch** — both machines run the identical PowerToys build.
- **Keyboard layout** — the received characters are always correct, only their order is wrong.
- **Resource leak** — handle counts rose during error bursts but were released again (1655 → 989 with no process restart), so this is not a monotonic leak.

With `UseService: true` the SYSTEM instances log outside the user profile:

```
C:\Windows\System32\config\systemprofile\AppData\Local\Microsoft\PowerToys\
    MouseWithoutBorders\Logs\<version>\<guid>Log_<yyyy-MM-dd>.log
```

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I would like to propose a lightweight PowerToys utility called **Lock Screen Notes**, allowing users to display a short, user-defined note directly on the Windows lock screen (Win + L).

Unlike desktop Sticky Notes or conventional widgets, the primary goal is to make personal reminders visible **before unlocking the computer**.

The proposed MVP would include:

- A simple text editor for one short note.
- Display on the actual Windows lock screen.
- Automatic content updates without manually generating wallpapers.
- An option to enable or disable the feature.
- Local storage without requiring cloud services.
- A privacy warning, since lock-screen content is visible to others.
- Graceful handling of unsupported Windows versions.

This is not intended to become a complete sticky-notes application or a general-purpose lock-screen customization tool.

### Scenario when this would be used

Examples include:

- “Remember to bring the documents before leaving.”
- “Review the open PR before the meeting.”
- “Pick up the parcel on the way home.”

Currently, these reminders are usually placed on the desktop, where they are hidden when Windows is locked.

### Possible technical implementation

Windows 11 supports third-party widgets on the lock screen. A potential implementation could use a Windows App SDK widget provider with a small Adaptive Card.

However, this approach requires further investigation, particularly regarding:

- Actual visibility and refresh behavior after Win + L.
- Supported Windows versions and editions.
- Widget registration and packaging compatibility with PowerToys.
- Privacy, security, and lifecycle management.

The implementation should rely on documented Windows APIs rather than injecting into system processes or bypassing lock-screen security.

### Questions for maintainers

1. Would a focused utility like this fit the PowerToys project?
2. Would a small proof of concept be welcome before implementing a complete module?
3. Would the team prefer this as a standalone Windows widget rather than an integrated PowerToy?

### Related issues

- #33066 — Personalization Lockscreen
- #37836 — Add Live Widgets to Windows 11 Desktop
- #25299 — Adding video wallpaper and widgets

I would be interested in contributing to the implementation if the maintainers consider this an appropriate direction.

Off by default, with a strength control (and ideally a choice of frost / dim). The 0.97 appearance options (background image, blur, tint) only affect the palette's own window. Nothing affects the rest of the screen, so the palette still sits on top of busy, high-contrast windows and is harder to read and focus on than launchers that dim the desktop (e.g. Spotlight, Raycast). ### Scenario when this would be used? Opening the palette over a dense workspace (multiple monitors, IDE, spreadsheets, video calls). Frosting the background makes the palette the clear focus and cuts visual noise. It would be used every time the palette is invoked, so it needs to appear instantly and add no noticeable delay. ### Supporting information

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.102.2862.0 - Preview (Insider)

### Installation method

Other (please specify in "Steps to Reproduce")

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Utilities

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run PowerToys normally (not as administrator) with Mouse Utilities > Auto Hide Cursor enabled and "hide while typing" on (its default once the utility is on).
2. Press Win+X, then A, to open Terminal (Admin). Any elevated window works.
3. The A keypress hides the pointer. Move the mouse over the admin window.

Also reproducible with "hide when idle": with an elevated window in front, leave the mouse still until the pointer hides, then move it.

Installation: per-user install, kept current by PowerToys auto-update with prerelease updates on.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The pointer reappears as soon as the mouse moves, as it does when a normal (non-elevated) window is in front.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The pointer stays invisible everywhere (the system cursors stay transparent) until a non-elevated window gets focus, for example by right-clicking the taskbar. Opening the same Terminal without admin (Win+X, I) is fine.

Measured on this machine (mouse moves injected from an elevated helper; pointer state read from the current cursor's mask bitmap):

| Window in front | After idle | After moving the mouse | WH_MOUSE_LL hook at medium integrity saw | GetCursorPos at medium integrity saw the move |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Normal app | Hidden | Visible | 6 of 6 moves | Yes |
| Windows Terminal (admin) | Hidden | Still hidden | 0 of 6 moves | Yes |

Likely cause: `AutoHideCursorWorker` only restores the pointer from its `WH_MOUSE_LL` hook (`MouseHookProc` -> `State::OnMouseInput`). When PowerToys runs at medium integrity and a high-integrity window is in the foreground, UIPI keeps the low-level hooks from being called, so Show never fires. Because `SetSystemCursor` is global, the pointer is gone in every app, not only the elevated one.

Possible fixes: restore from the existing 100 ms timer when `GetCursorPos` shows the pointer has moved since it was hidden (`GetCursorPos` still sees the movement here); or don't hide while an elevated window is in the foreground; or at least list Auto Hide Cursor among the utilities that need PowerToys running as administrator.

Workarounds: restart PowerToys as administrator (confirmed to fix it here), or turn Auto Hide Cursor off.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

- Windows 11 Home 26H2, build 26300.9711
- .NET Windows Desktop runtime 10.0.11
- System language: en-GB
- User installation; PowerToys not running as admin when this happens
- Elevation on this machine happens without a UAC prompt; the hide-when-idle repro doesn't depend on that

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

When using PowerToys Peek to preview image files, it would be helpful if the preview window displayed basic image metadata, including:
Image dimensions (e.g., 1920 × 1080 px)
File size
Image format (JPG, PNG, WebP, etc.)
Optional: DPI and color profile

### Scenario when this would be used?

Many users rely on Peek as a quick alternative to opening images in an editor. When reviewing large numbers of marketing, web, or product images, knowing the dimensions immediately is often the primary piece of information needed.

### Supporting information

Use Case
Many users rely on Peek as a quick alternative to opening images in an editor. When reviewing large numbers of marketing, web, or product images, knowing the dimensions immediately is often the primary piece of information needed.

Current Behavior
Peek displays the image preview but does not show dimensions or other image metadata.

Requested Behavior
Add an option in Peek settings to display image metadata either:
In a small information bar at the bottom of the preview window, or
As an optional overlay that can be toggled on/off.

Benefits
Faster image review workflows
Reduced need to open Properties or an image editor

body_text: ### Microsoft PowerToys version 0.101.2362.0 ### Installation method PowerToys auto-update ### Area(s) with issue? Command Palette ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open Command Palette (Win+Alt+Space). 2. Type the exact query `open environment variables`. 3. Observe the result ordering. ### Expected Behavior Since the query is an exact (or near-exact) textual match of the fallback command's title "Open Environment Variables", it should rank at or near the top of the results list, directly launchable with Enter. ### Actual Behavior The matching fallback commands ("Open Environment Variables", "Open Environment Variables (Admin)", "Environment Variables") are pushed into a separate, lower-priority "Fallbacks" section below unrelated, non-matching results such as "Run command" and "Search the web in Firefox". This means an exact textual match requires an extra keypress (Down Arrow) instead of a direct Enter. In the PowerToys Settings UI, this release is advertised as "PowerToys Run's evolution". For this very common scenario (opening the Environment Variables editor), the actual user experience is a clear regression compared to the previous PowerToys Run plugin behavior, where a fallback with this level of match confidence was shown as the top result reachable with a single Enter press. ### Additional Information This appears related to the general fallback scoring/ranking issue discussed in #40080 ("Add match score hint to fallback items") and #44630 ("Cmdpal fallback ranking", closed). Those discussions concluded that fallback items currently lack an "exact match" confidence signal, causing generic results to consistently outrank highly relevant fallback commands even on literal title matches. This issue demonstrates a concrete, reproducible case of that gap for the built-in Environment Variables fallback. Screenshots illustrating the issue are attached below (query `env var` and the exact query `open environment variables`, both showing the relevant fallback ranked last). ### Other Software _No response_

body_text:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

This little utility called [CopyTap](https://copytap.netlify.app/) showed up on Hacker News and seems like the perfect kind of thing to integrate into PowerToys. It implements three independent clipboards, each accessed using the traditional Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V shortcuts but differentiated by pressing C or V one, two, or three times while holding Ctrl.

In other words, clipboard one works the same as usual, but for clipboard two, you press Ctrl+C C to copy to it and Ctrl+V V to paste from it. Clipboard three uses Ctrl+C C C and Ctrl+V V V. Each clipboard is independent so you can store different things or different types of things in each.

It would also be useful to have the ability to cut to each clipboard as well. It doesn't appear that CopyTap supports that.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Just as an example of how this would be useful, I've recently been working on a photo book in Affinity Publisher. I have master pages with empty picture frames in multiple layouts. As I'm adding photos, I often need to rearrange the photos on the page. Affinity doesn't let you just drag photos between frames, so I have to cut and paste between them.

If the page is full, I don't have a temporary place to move one photo to open up a space to move the others around (sort of like a classic number sliding  puzzle). So, I end up deleting one photo, re-arrange the others, and then finding and re-adding the deleted photo.

With this feature, I could just cut one photo to clipboard two, rearrange the others as usual with clipboard one, and then paste the cut photo from clipboard two when I'm done.

I could probably use clipboard history, but it's not as quick or intuitive as this would be. I'd have to scroll through the history to find the right photo to re-add at the end instead of just pressing Ctrl+V V.

As I'm adding photos, I often need to rearrange the photos on the page. Affinity doesn't let you just drag photos between frames, so I have to cut and paste between them.

If the page is full, I don't have a temporary place to move one photo to open up a space to move the others around (sort of like a classic number sliding  puzzle). So, I end up deleting one photo, re-arrange the others, and then finding and re-adding the deleted photo.

With this feature, I could just cut one photo to clipboard two, rearrange the others as usual with clipboard one, and then paste the cut photo from clipboard two when I'm done.

I could probably use clipboard history, but it's not as quick or intuitive as this would be. I'd have to scroll through the history to find the right photo to re-add at the end instead of just pressing Ctrl+V V.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Add a customizable global keyboard shortcut to fully enable and disable the Mouse Pointer Crosshairs module directly. This would allow users to toggle the feature's system-level state without having to navigate through the main PowerToys settings user interface.

### Scenario when this would be used?

During software development, it is frequently necessary to capture clean screenshots of UI elements, such as application menus and nested submenus. Currently, the active crosshair obstructs the screen capture. This forces a disruption in the workflow: opening the PowerToys settings, manually disabling the crosshair module, capturing the screen, and then returning to the settings to re-enable it. A dedicated shortcut would allow for instant toggling right before and after taking a screen capture.

### Supporting information

While PowerToys already includes a default activation shortcut (Win + Alt + P) to show or hide the crosshairs, the overlay can sometimes still interfere with screen capture tools or accidentally trigger during rapid development tasks. Providing a quick shortcut to disable the module entirely ensures the capture environment is clean, preventing the need to continuously manage the PowerToys GUI while documenting software.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Shortcut Guide picks a manifest by the foreground window's process name (`WindowFilter`). Web apps installed from Chromium-based browsers (PWAs such as YouTube, YouTube Music, Outlook, Teams) all run inside `chrome.exe` / `msedge.exe`, so the guide always shows the browser's shortcuts for them, even though each web app has its own, completely different shortcuts.

Each web app window does carry its own AppUserModelID (for example `Chrome._crx_<app id>`). That's the same identity Windows uses to give web apps their own taskbar button. A normal browser window just reports `Chrome` / `MSEdge`.

Proposal: add an optional `AppUserModelId` field to the keyboard shortcuts manifest schema:

```yaml
PackageName: +Google.YouTubeMusic
Name: YouTube Music
WindowFilter: "chrome.exe"
AppUserModelId: "Chrome._crx_cinhimbnkkghhklpknlkffjgod*"
BackgroundProcess: false
Shortcuts: ...
```

- A manifest with `AppUserModelId` only applies to foreground windows whose AppUserModelID matches (`;`-separated, case-insensitive, trailing `*` = prefix match for profile suffixes).
- It takes precedence over manifests that match the same `WindowFilter` by process name only, so a normal Chrome window still shows Chrome's shortcuts.
- Manifests without the field behave exactly as today, and `index.yml` is unchanged for them.
- The nav item uses the web app window's own icon instead of the browser's.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Anyone who uses web apps as installed apps (YouTube, YouTube Music, Outlook on the web, Teams, Spotify, Discord, and many more). Today pressing the Shortcut Guide hotkey over them shows Chrome/Edge tab shortcuts that mostly don't apply in an app window, and none of the app's own shortcuts.

### Supporting information

I have a working implementation with unit tests and have validated it locally against the installed v0.101.2362 with YouTube and YouTube Music web apps. I'll link a draft PR here for discussion. Happy to change the approach (for example, field name or matching rules) based on feedback.

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

Preview v0.102.2883.0

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

Command Palette

### Steps to reproduce

Enable the Command Palette Dock.
Set the appearance mode to Dark.
Restart PowerToys / Command Palette.
Observe the dark text on the dark Dock background.
Open the Dock settings without modifying anything.
The text immediately changes to white.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The Dock should correctly initialize the foreground color according to the selected Dark theme.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The Dock initially displays dark text. Opening the settings triggers a visual refresh and fixes the text color.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

The issue persists after testing a different background configuration.
Possibly related: #45998.
The behavior suggests that the foreground theme resources are not correctly initialized on startup and are refreshed when opening the settings.

### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

v0.101.2362

### Installation method

GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Utilities

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Mouse Highlighter settings and set the highlight mode to **Ripple**.
2. In the **Primary** (or **Secondary**) color picker, type or paste an RGBA hex value into the hex input, for example:
   - 6-digit: `#3366CC`
   - 8-digit: `#3366CC80`

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The hex input reads values in RGBA order (`#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`), matching the hex notation defined in CSS Color Module Level 4.

- `#3366CC` → R `33`, G `66`, B `CC`, A `FF` (alpha defaults to fully opaque when omitted)
- `#3366CC80` → R `33`, G `66`, B `CC`, A `80`

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The hex input reads values in ARGB order (`#AARRGGBB`), so every channel shifts one position:

- `#3366CC` → A `33`, R `66`, G `CC`, B `00` (blue is forced to `00`, and the first byte becomes alpha)
- `#3366CC80` → A `33`, R `66`, G `CC`, B `80`

The resulting color differs from the one entered, and pasting colors from design tools, CSS, or other apps produces the wrong hue and unintended transparency.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[PowerToysReport_2026-10-16-11-02-57.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33552637/PowerToysReport_2026-10-16-11-02-57.zip)

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

SupersedingAsyncGate serializes three operations in CmdPal: 
- reloading top-level commands (TopLevelCommandManager), 
- saving the provider cache (DefaultCommandProviderCache), 
- saving bookmarks (BookmarksManager). 
 
Its contract is superseding: a new call cancels the in-flight operation and completes earlier callers as canceled.

None of the three callers needs that. They all ignore the cancellation token (the saves on purpose, since stopping a file write halfway is unsafe), and none awaits the result in production. What they need is coalescing: one run at a time, with requests that arrive during a run sharing a follow-up run. 

---

Proposed replacement `CoalescingAsyncRunner` with following contract, matching issues we encountered:

- Execution: Only one run at a time, always in the background. RequestAsync() must never call the delegate inline because BookmarksManager requests saves under its lock, and the write itself is synchronous.
- Batching: Each request joins the next run that hasn't started. Requests arriving during a run share one follow-up; requests during that follow-up go into the next batch. New requests can't keep pushing older ones back.
- Completion: Once accepted, work stays queued. Each request's task gets its run's outcome, including faults or cancellation from the delegate. Either way, the next batch still runs. RequestAsync() takes no cancellation token; callers can use Task.WaitAsync() to limit their wait.
- Idle: WhenIdleAsync() waits until nothing is running or pending. It doesn't report whether saves succeeded; both save delegates already catch and log write failures.
- Busy: IsBusy is set under the lock when a request is accepted and cleared when the worker finds no work left. The worker sends notifications in order, outside the lock. It keeps ownership through the idle notification, then checks for more work under the lock before stepping down. Handler exceptions are caught so they can't skip that check. This means the worker can still be active while IsBusy is false.
- Disposal: Disposal stops accepting requests, returning canceled tasks for new calls. Accepted work finishes normally. DisposeAsync() also waits for the final notification, so the owner can safely tear down afterward.
- Locking: No user code or task continuations run under the internal lock.

### Scenario when this would be used?

DevExp, reliability

body_text: ### Description of the new feature / enhancement Windows arranges monitors in one virtual desktop measured in pixels. With monitors of different size or resolution, that layout cannot match the desk, which causes two problems. **1. The pointer jumps when it crosses between monitors.** When the pointer crosses a shared border, Windows keeps the pixel coordinate along that border. With different pixel densities or physical offsets, it leaves one screen at one physical spot and enters the other somewhere else. Example: a 27" 4K monitor (≈0.156 mm per pixel) with a 24" 1080p monitor (≈0.277 mm per pixel) above it. Windows thinks the 24" covers 50 % of the 4K monitor's top edge; physically it covers ≈89 %. At best one point along the border is correct. 1000 px away from it, the pointer lands ≈120 mm from where you expect it. The Windows setting **Ease cursor movement between displays** (the reason #1226 was closed) does not solve this. It only lets the pointer jump over spots where it would get stuck. It does not keep the physical position, so the jump is still there (see the screenshots in #40296 and #43427). **2. Monitors that touch on the desk can be apart in the layout, and the pointer cannot cross between them.** Example: a 32" 4K and a 27" 1440p monitor stand side by side on a 57" super-ultrawide. On the desk they touch each other and together cover about 93 % of the wide monitor's width. In pixels they are 3840 + 2560 = 6400 px wide, against the wide monitor's 7680 px. Place each one above the spot where it physically stands, and the layout has a gap of about 800 px between them. Windows does not connect monitors that do not touch in the layout, so the pointer cannot move from the 32" to the 27" right next to it: you go down to the wide monitor and back up. Closing the gap in the layout instead moves the 27" away from where it stands, and every crossing between it and the wide monitor jumps sideways. Windows cannot have both. Proposal: a new Mouse Utility, **Seamless Multi-Screen Cursor**, off by default. * **Calibration without measuring.** A full-screen overlay shows two numbered pairs of lines across every shared border. The user drags the lines of each pair until they look like one straight line running across the bezel. Two pairs fix both the scale and the offset of the border, with no sizes or millimeters to type in. Initial positions are predicted from the monitors' EDID sizes. A **Try while adjusting** switch applies the lines live, and an optional pointer trail shows whether a move across the border stays straight. * **Remapping at runtime.** A low-level mouse hook remaps the pointer only at the moment it crosses a calibrated border, so movement is physically continuous. Movement inside a monitor is not touched. * **Glue monitors across gaps.** Two monitors that face each other across a gap in the layout, with no monitor in between, get a **Glue** switch. Once glued, the pair is calibrated like a shared border, and the pointer crosses the gap directly, at the same physical height, as if the monitors touched in the layout too. So the layout can stay where the monitors really are: in the example above, every crossing between the three monitors is straight, including from the part of the wide monitor's top edge under the gap. * **Per-border control.** Each border has a **Smooth crossing** switch. Where no monitor is physically across, the pointer can stop at the edge, as at the edge of a real screen (option). * **Robust.** The calibration is stored relative to each monitor, keyed by device path, so it survives re-arranging monitors in Windows display settings and resolution changes. Rotated or missing monitors fall back to the Windows behavior. Games that confine (`ClipCursor`) or hide the pointer, pen and touch input are left alone. * **Works with CursorWrap.** Calibrated borders, including the edges of a glued pair, never wrap, and CursorWrap wraps can keep the physical position (option). * **Full PowerToys integration:** Settings page, GPO, OOBE, Quick Access, a Command Palette command to open the calibration, and telemetry with no monitor identifiers, sizes or positions. I have a working implementation, with a spec, developer docs and unit tests, and will link a draft PR here. Would the team accept this as a new Mouse Utility? ### Scenario when this would be used? Anyone with monitors of different sizes or pixel densities side by side or stacked, which is very common: 1. A laptop (small, high-DPI) docked under or next to a large external monitor. Moving the pointer up from the laptop should come out at the same physical spot on the big monitor, not far to the left. 2. A 4K and a 1440p monitor of different sizes side by side, bottoms aligned on the desk. Crossing left or right should keep the pointer at the same height. 3. A super-ultrawide with two smaller monitors standing on it, or any desk where monitors touch physically but cannot touch in the layout. Glued, the pointer moves straight from one upper monitor to the other, and every crossing to the wide monitor continues straight up or down. 4. Someone who re-arranges the monitors in display settings. The calibration still applies; only physically moving a monitor needs recalibration. 5. Someone who wants the Windows behavior on one border (for example to a TV). They switch that border off; the other borders stay seamless. Today the only fix is a third-party tool. LittleBigMouse is the best known; it needs a millimeter layout of all monitors typed in by hand. ### Supporting information Related requests: #1226 (closed as built into Windows), #36432 and #39916 (closed), #43427, #50051, #30315, #35891, and #40296 (crossing gaps; gluing covers monitors that face each other, not diagonal corners). Prior art: [LittleBigMouse](https://github.com/mgth/littlebigmouse) (GPL-3.0). It was used as a reference for ideas only; no code is copied. The main difference is the calibration: two drags per border instead of a hand-made millimeter layout. Screenshots of the calibration overlay (rendered for made-up layouts): 1. The gap example above: a 57" super-ultrawide (7680 × 2160) with a 32" 4K and a 27" 1440p monitor standing on it. Each border has its color and two line pairs; the two upper monitors are glued across the gap between them (green lines and **Glue** switches). The colored edge map shows where the pointer crosses (border color), stops (red) or is left to Windows. 2. Mixed orientation and display scale. 3. Gaps on several sides: every pair that faces across a gap with nothing in between is offered for gluing. 4. The pointer trail across a remapped crossing, and the line drawn when CursorWrap wraps the pointer.
